articles.title: Oura adds new fitness metrics to show how workouts impact your body | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
As competition in the smart ring market escalates, Oura is introducing two new features to give people more insight into their workouts and how they impact their bodies. The company announced on Tuesday it’s rolling out Cardio Effort and VO₂ max metrics to expand workout tracking beyond exercise duration and heart rate zones.
While Oura has largely dominated the smart ring market for years, rivals like RingConn and Ultrahuman are emerging to dethrone it, putting pressure on the company to keep innovating. By launching more advanced workout metrics, Oura is looking to differentiate itself from competitors.
With Cardio Effort, users will be able to see how much a workout taxes their cardiovascular system. This measurement is aggregated over the week relative to each user’s individual baseline to provide more insights. Oura explained that this metric shifts users’ focus from “How many minutes did I move?” to “Am I maintaining my fitness, building it, or overdoing it?”
Since Cardio Effort accounts for both intensity and duration, a shorter, more intense workout can yield a similar score to a longer, less intense one, the company says.
Oura notes that the metric has two components: Workout Cardio Effort and Weekly Cardio Effort. The first metric evaluates the impact of an individual workout, while the latter aggregates effort into a weekly total, categorized as “Light,” “Fair,” “Maintaining,” “Building,” or “Reaching.”

articles.title: Elon Musk diz que IA e robôs são única saída para dívida dos EUA
articles.summary:
Elon Musk afirmou que a inteligência artificial (IA) e os robôs são a única maneira de resolver o problema da dívida pública dos Estados Unidos, que atingiu US$ 40 trilhões (cerca de R$ 216 trilhões) em agosto. Para o bilionário, tentar equilibrar as contas do governo apenas por meio de cortes de gastos não é uma estratégia viável.
A declaração foi feita em episódio recém-publicado do podcast The Builders, apresentado pelo escritor Walter Isaacson. Durante a conversa, Musk contou que chegou a essa conclusão após seus 130 dias como funcionário especial do governo na segunda administração de Donald Trump.
Entre janeiro e maio de 2025, o empresário liderou, na prática, o escritório de Eficiência Governamental da Casa Branca, conhecido como DOGE, que tinha como objetivo reduzir os gastos federais.
“Cheguei à conclusão de que a única maneira de resolver a dívida nacional é com IA e robôs. Não vamos conseguir resolvê-la tentando economizar até chegar lá”, disse Musk a Isaacson. O empresário classificou essa última possibilidade como “impossível”.

articles.title: Hacker übernehmen CDU-Mailkonto und verschicken 6.500 Phishing-Nachrichten – auch an Kanzler Merz
articles.summary:
Hacker übernehmen CDU-Mailkonto und verschicken 6.500 Phishing-Nachrichten – auch an Kanzler Merz
In den vergangenen Tagen haben zahlreiche Politiker:innen der CDU eine oder sogar mehrere E-Mails erhalten, auf die sie lieber nicht klicken sollten. Denn statt echter interner Kommunikation handelte es sich dabei um getarnte Phishing-Mails von Hacker:innen. Sie hatten es geschafft, sich Zugang zu echten E-Mail-Adressen von CDU-Politiker:innen zu verschaffen und darüber betrügerische Nachrichten zu verschicken.
Phishing-Mail an Merz: Was in den Nachrichten stand
Wie Heise berichtet, hatten sich die Hacker:innen Zugriff auf das Konto des Geschäftsführers des CDU-Kreisverbands in Heilbronn verschafft. Wie es dazu kam, ist bislang nicht final geklärt. Möglich wäre, dass auch der Geschäftsführer zunächst Opfer einer Phishing-Mail geworden ist. Sicher ist, dass sie Angreifer:innen das Konto im Anschluss genutzt haben, um mehr als 6.500 Mails an CDU-Politiker:innen in ganz Deutschland zu verschicken, darunter auch Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz.
Nachdem der Vorfall entdeckt wurde, hat der CDU-Kreisverband das Landeskriminalamt eingeschaltet. Noch ermittelt die Polizei, ob es unter den Empfänger:innen jemanden gab, der betrügerische Mails geöffnet hat. Die Mails lockten unter anderem mit vermeintlichen echten Betreffzeilen wie „Einladung zur 19. Böckinger Prominentenpredigt“ oder „Ummeldung / … / CDU SBK zu CDU Neckarsulm“.

articles.title: Super Mario Galaxy, cuántas horas dura y cómo usarlo en Android: hasta 1440p a 60 FPS
articles.summary:
Super Mario Galaxy ya puede ejecutarse de forma nativa en teléfonos Android sin recurrir a un emulador. El responsable es Galaxy Android, un port no oficial que aprovecha la reciente decompilación completa del código fuente del juego de Wii para funcionar mediante Vulkan y AAudio, con la posibilidad de alcanzar hasta 120 cuadros por segundo en dispositivos móviles.
En paralelo, para quienes busquen la máxima calidad visual, el emulador Dolphin en computadora sigue siendo una vía para jugarlo a 1440p y 60 FPS estables.
Cuánto dura Super Mario Galaxy según el estilo de juego
La extensión de la aventura depende de qué tan a fondo se quiera explorar. Completar la historia principal y derrotar a Bowser toma entre 13 y 15 horas. Quienes además busquen estrellas adicionales y recorran la mayoría de las galaxias pueden extender la experiencia a entre 20 y 25 horas.
Para quienes apuntan al 100%, el desafío es mayor: reunir las 120 estrellas con Mario, desbloquear a Luigi y repetir la hazaña con el segundo personaje (240 estrellas en total) demanda entre 35 y 42 horas de juego.
Cómo correr Super Mario Galaxy en Android sin emulador
El desarrollo de Galaxy Android fue posible después de que, a finales de septiembre, Super Mario Galaxy se convirtiera en el primer título de Nintendo Wii en ser decompilado por completo. Le secrétaire américain au Commerce s’était pourtant opposé publiquement, dès le mois d’août, à l’idée de voir de la mémoire chinoise équiper les produits des grands groupes du pays. articles.title: Votre vieille Radeon et votre Xbox s’offrent une seconde jeunesse : AMD déploie le FSR 4.1 avec des mois d’avance — Frandroid
articles.summary:
AMD a publié ce mardi 20 octobre le pilote Adrenalin 26.10.1, qui active le FSR 4.1 sur les Radeon RX 6000, des cartes graphiques sorties en 2020. La marque l’annonce dans un billet et une vidéo qui couvrent aussi les PC portables, les consoles portables et les Xbox. Jusqu’ici, seules les RX 9000 et, depuis juin, les Radeon RX 7000 y avaient droit. Avec une RX 6600 ou une RX 6800, on obtient donc une image plus propre dans les jeux compatibles, sans changer de carte.
Le FSR (FidelityFX Super Resolution) fait calculer au jeu une image dans une définition plus basse, puis la remonte à celle de l’écran. Le gain d’images par seconde vient de là. Depuis la version 4, AMD confie cette reconstruction à un modèle d’apprentissage automatique entraîné à retrouver les détails, alors que le FSR 3.1 utilisait un algorithme classique. L’image obtenue est plus nette, avec moins de scintillement sur les bords des objets.
Pourquoi ce délai pour les RX 6000 ? Le modèle a été pensé pour les RX 9000, qui calculent nativement en FP8, un format de nombres sur 8 bits. Les cartes plus anciennes passent par une variante en INT8, un format différent, ce qui demande un travail d’adaptation. En mai, AMD visait encore « début 2027 » pour ces cartes. L’entreprise dit avoir retravaillé le modèle et optimisé son code pour leur architecture, RDNA 2. Le pilote couvre toute la gamme, de la RX 6900 à la RX 6400.

At OCP 2026, we saw the new NVIDIA BlueField-4 STX Server for Context Memory (CMX). Partners had been asking for this, and NVIDIA delivered. Onboard, we have a lower-cost design than the dual-Vera setup we saw previously. Let us take a look at the new board.
NVIDIA BlueField-4 STX Server for CMX at OCP 2026
For context, this is the previously shown BlueField-4 DPU. That one, pictured below, is a dual Vera CPU setup, each with SOCAMM memory, plus four ConnectX-9 SuperNICs. NVIDIA calls this a DPU, but it is clearly more costly than a BlueField-1 or BlueField-3, which are much smaller and lower-power devices. For partners looking at building storage platforms, the below is more akin to a dual CPU server than a traditional DPU.
At OCP 2026, multiple partners showed off the BlueField-4 STX server for context memory (CMX). Here is the much smaller card, which still uses high-density connectors for PCIe and system connectivity.
NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs encompass both NVIDIA Grace and Vera CPU cores, but this one looks like a Vera package. That is a very substantial CPU. To be clear, this is not like the embedded-class CPUs that we typically have seen in DPUs previously. This is more like having a high-end single-socket server platform.
Another interesting feature is that the boards at OCP 2026 are using SOCAMM memory, so these should be relatively easy to put either a heatsink or a liquid cooling block on top of it.

articles.title: Introducing tsrs: a Port of TypeScript to Rust
articles.summary:
Introducing tsrs: A port of TypeScript to Rust
Cloudflare and VoidZero are now working with Max Schwenk of Owner.com on tsrs, a Rust port of the TypeScript compiler. We are doing this work in close collaboration with the TypeScript team, and incubating tsrs as part of the Oxc JavaScript compiler toolchain.
Our goal is to help developers spend less time waiting for their code to be checked and more time building. Making TypeScript faster and more memory-efficient also helps bring complete development environments to more places, including right in your browser.
To be clear, we are not forking TypeScript. We believe the TypeScript team should remain in full control of the language’s design and direction. They have maintained a long-term vision while guiding TypeScript’s adoption across the JavaScript community. We do not want to change that.
The TypeScript team can move quite fast on many things, but for some features they may spend years intentionally exploring options and making prototypes before picking the right implementation. A Rust port has to follow those decisions closely, or it will eventually fall apart and become incompatible. We have to preserve the TypeScript language strictly based on its original implementation – and the TypeScript team should remain solely responsible for deciding what that looks like.
Performance and memory improvements

articles.title: Build a semantic layer for agentic AI on AWS with AtScale and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Build a semantic layer for agentic AI on AWS with AtScale and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
In the first post in this series, we built a semantic layer on AWS using Stardog’s knowledge graph over Amazon Aurora and Amazon Redshift. We ran a Strands agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore against that layer. The second post kept the same customer 360 (C360) pattern and swapped in Denodo’s data virtualization platform, extending the source mix to include an on-premises PostgreSQL cluster. This post uses the same C360 pattern again, with AtScale as the semantic layer.
AtScale takes a different shape from the first two. The semantic model is dimensional (dimensions, hierarchies, and measures) rather than a graph of triples or a set of views. AtScale authors the model in the Semantic Modeling Language, an open, YAML-based specification versioned in Git, and exposes it simultaneously, from a single deployed model, over three protocols: SQL, XML for Analysis (XMLA), and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The Strands agent and the business intelligence (BI) tools the enterprise already uses get the same computed answer from the same definitions.
The rest of the pattern carries over from the earlier posts. A foundation model on Amazon Bedrock (Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.6 for the walkthrough) plans and writes queries. articles.title: Xbox CEO is reportedly planning three more rounds of layoffs
articles.summary:
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma is planning new rounds of layoffs for sometime this month, November, and January, according to Fortune. In July, as part of an organizational “reset,” Sharma announced planned layoffs affecting 3,200 staffers over the course of Microsoft’s 2027 fiscal year, including 1,600 cuts at that time, and in September, Microsoft laid off around 260 employees. Sharma’s changes have also included letting Double Fine and Compulsion Games become independent again, though Senua developer Ninja Theory may close.
Xbox CEO is reportedly planning three more rounds of layoffs
Microsoft may lay off Xbox staff this month, in November, and in January.
The report also touches on speculation that Xbox may be spun off or sold, and Judson Althoff, the CEO of Microsoft’s commercial business, seemed to downplay that idea to Fortune. “Asha is one of the best leaders we have at the whole company,” Althoff said to Fortune. “We would not have put her on a business we intend to sell. There’s going to be a ton of speculation about all this. Time will tell.”
Sharma recently told The New York Times that “Xbox is not for sale.”
Fortune’s report also said that Microsoft is planning to launch a “next-generation handheld device” in 2027 and its Project Helix console in 2028.

articles.title: Spotify launches paid podcast memberships with perks beyond bonus content | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Spotify on Tuesday launched paid memberships, a new way for podcasters to make money from their biggest fans beyond paywalled bonus episodes. Creators can decide which perks to offer listeners, which could be bonus audio or video, fewer ads, early access to shows, or some combination of these.
The streaming service first previewed the idea at its Investor Day in May, where it also introduced AI capabilities that let listeners ask questions about what they’re listening to or watching and debuted new tools for managing creator sponsorships.
As the company explained at the time, memberships would help to “create a natural path to go deeper, unlocking new and exclusive experiences for fans and new revenue opportunities for creators.”
The feature is now rolling out to 34 markets globally, including the U.S.
The launch is the latest example of Spotify’s effort to make its platform more attractive to podcast creators, particularly as it moves further into the video space to compete with YouTube. Though podcasters have long been able to monetize through ads, the new memberships could entice more fans to support creators by offering more than just an occasional bonus episode.
Creators keep 90% of the membership revenue and can package their benefits across multiple tiers and pricing options to appeal to fans at different levels of commitment. To qualify, podcasters must host their shows on Spotify for Creators or Megaphone, have at least 100 consumption hours, 100 listeners or viewers…

articles.title: XUPER TV Conecta y deportes En Vivo: por qué se busca en Google y no es recomendado
articles.summary:
“XUPER TV Conecta” y “deportes En Vivo” son algunas de las búsquedas que más crecen entre quienes quieren ver series, películas y eventos deportivos sin pagar suscripciones. La aplicación, antes conocida como Magis TV, circula fuera de las tiendas oficiales y se instala de forma manual en televisores, TV Box y celulares con Android.
Según un análisis de ESET, ese método de distribución puede comprometer el funcionamiento del dispositivo y exponer datos personales de los usuarios.
El interés por “XUPER TV Conecta” y “deportes En Vivo” no se limita a la calidad de la transmisión. El verdadero riesgo aparece en los permisos que estas plataformas solicitan para funcionar, muchos de los cuales exceden lo necesario para reproducir contenido. Esos accesos pueden facilitar la lectura de archivos privados, la instalación de otros programas sin aviso y el envío de notificaciones engañosas.
Por qué buscar “XUPER TV Conecta” y “deportes En Vivo” implica un riesgo
Quienes buscan “XUPER TV Conecta” y “deportes En Vivo” suelen llegar a páginas web, enlaces compartidos en redes sociales o grupos de mensajería. Ese circuito evita los procesos de revisión que aplican Google Play Store, App Store y otros catálogos oficiales antes de habilitar una descarga.
La ausencia de esos controles permite que el archivo descargado incluya funciones no informadas al usuario. Es posible que el enlace lleve a una versión modificada de la aplicación, con malware incorporado desde el origen.

articles.title: Mozilla asks UK CMA to consult on browser choice screens now | The Mozilla Blog
articles.summary:
Why is the CMA asking us to choose the furniture before the house? The UK’s search choice screens need browser choice screens alongside them
Mobile browsers are a key gateway to the internet for 56 million people in the UK. Smartphone users spend around half an hour a day in these apps, and opening a browser is the most common way they look up information online.
Yet most people are using a smartphone browser that was preinstalled and set as the default for them, without ever being asked which browser they would actually prefer.
Mozilla believes people deserve an active choice in the tools they depend on every day, which is why the latest proposals from the UK Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) matter. We welcome the CMA’s plans to give people a choice of search service and are asking it to consult on browser choice now, so both screens can launch together.
On September 23rd, the CMA published updated plans that would require Google to show people in the UK a choice of search service on new Android devices, covering the default search app and home-screen search widget as well as Chrome. Search choice screens would also appear in Chrome on other platforms, including through a major update for existing users. Some AI assistants would also be eligible to appear alongside search engines.
The proposals are well designed, but solve only half the problem

articles.title: A cleaner path to rare earth metals
articles.summary:
A cleaner path to rare earth metals
Tomás Villalón Jr. ’14
Tomás Villalón Jr. ’14 was raised in San Antonio, Texas, but vividly remembers smog hanging over the city his family came from—Monterrey, Mexico, a steel manufacturing and metal fabrication hub. Even as a child, he realized it was problematic to breathe that air.
“I’m motivated because I’ve seen what metal-making does,” says Villalón, who majored in materials science and engineering. He started thinking about sustainable metallurgy senior year while working at Boston Metal, an MIT spinoff focused on decarbonizing steelmaking. In 2019 he cofounded Phoenix Tailings, which has developed an efficient process for extracting rare earth metals from mining waste.
“The mining ecosystem by itself makes over several billion tons of waste,” says Villalón, who serves as chief technology officer. (Others on the founding team are Michelle Chao ’17, Nick Myers, and Anthony Balladon.) “We have to get rid of this pollution.”
The company asserts that its proprietary electrochemical technique for processing rare earths generates no toxins and is carbon-free when fueled by renewables.

Plinto was founded in early 2025 by Nermina Suljevic, Nielsen, and Sebastian Rehnby, who previously worked for Peakon, the employee engagement platform acquired by US-based Workday in 2021. The company’s CTO Andreas Garnæs is also an alumnus of Peakon. Together, they bring experience across product development, engineering, commercial scaling, and working with large international organisations.
In large organisations, the volume of financial transactions exceeds what finance teams can review manually. This work is handled by controllers, who typically resort to spot checks or end-of-month reconciliations, leaving enough room for errors such as incorrect prices, duplicate invoices, or mismatched deliveries.
Plinto wants to solve this problem with AI agents that sit on top of the systems companies already use, such as ERP, documents, bank, and collaboration tools like Slack or Microsoft Teams.

Mais c'est oublier la jurisprudence du Conseil d'État et le règlement européen sur les services numériques.

articles.title: Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
articles.summary:
Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- University of Oxford
- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. articles.title: A champion for brain injury patients
articles.summary:
A champion for brain injury patients
Alissa Totman ’13
Alissa Totman ’13 was a sophomore when she joined MIT BrainTrust, a student-run organization that connects Institute undergraduates and people with brain injuries for support and socializing. “That group was a great way to learn about the human experience of what people go through when they experience a brain injury,” she says. And it laid the foundation for her life’s work.
Today, Totman is a physician specializing in brain injury medicine at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center, where she treats adults with head trauma, stroke, brain tumors, and more.
She is also the founder of Synapse, a nonprofit focused on providing support for such individuals. The organization grew out of a group she started with Jaclyn Konopka ’14 during medical school at Stanford, and Totman launched it as a national service organization in 2016, while pursuing her master’s degree in public health at Harvard.
There are now chapters at 28 universities across the country—and Totman still runs the organization. “There’s a big need for more resources like this,” she says.

Companies are spending nearly a third of IT budgets on software upgrades
'Software tax' is a major ongoing cost
- Enterprises are being forced into software upgrades that they can't really get out of, report finds
- 91% have upgraded hardware in the past three years just to maintain software
- Enterprise protection legislation and software support obligations could be the answer
Legacy tech has become something of a hot topic in recent years with AI, but while hardware and data foundations have been core to the discussion around artificial intelligence, a new Origina report has revealed that around one-third of enterprise IT budgets are being earmarked for software upgrades.
The report found that 28% of large enterprise IT budgets are being spent on vendor-driven changes that they would not have otherwise chosen in a trend the company's calling a 'software tax'.
But more than just consuming budgets, software changes are also impacting worker time and leading to potentially lost productivity as a result.

articles.title: Inspired Capital closes $450M fourth fund as New York pushes back on Silicon Valley’s gravitational pull | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Inspired Capital, the early-stage firm founded in 2019 by Alexa von Tobel and Penny Pritzker, has closed its fourth fund with $450 million in commitments. The new capital will bring the firm’s assets under management to nearly $1.4 billion, von Tobel tells TechCrunch.
The raise comes as venture dollars are piling up on the West Coast. Between 2020 and the end of 2025, the Bay Area had raised $352 billion for VC funds — roughly 46% of all U.S. venture capital, according to PitchBook. Last year, that percentage shot up even higher, with Bay Area firms locking down 55% of the total new commitments to U.S. venture funds.
New York-based Inspired’s new fund is a reminder that capital is accruing elsewhere, too. In fact, Inspired is growing: it closed a $330 million third fund in early 2024, following a $281 million second fund and its $200 million debut fund.
Despite having money to invest, von Tobel says the firm is sticking to its formula. Inspired backs roughly 10 companies a year, which can be anywhere between “napkin” stage and Series A, writing checks between $1 million and $15 million. Pritzker, the former U.S. Commerce Secretary, remains an active co-founder in the firm.
With six years of investing experience under her belt, von Tobel is now willing to talk about results, too. articles.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
articles.summary:
AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
- Summary:
- A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.
- Share:
Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.
How Scientists Tested Perceptions of AI Consciousness

Paradigm Healthcare Services has told the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) that a data breach discovered last year affected more than 970,000 people.
San Francisco-based Paradigm processes billing for Medi-Cal, California’s Medicaid program, under a data use agreement with the California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS). It also maintains Medi-Cal member identification numbers on the department’s behalf.
The company says it became aware of unauthorized access to its local network on October 13, 2025. “On August 18, 2026, we determined that certain files containing select individuals’ protected health information may have been accessed by an unauthorized party between October 8, 2025, and October 15, 2025,” Paradigm said.
The compromised files contained names, dates of birth, gender, and Medi-Cal member identification numbers. Paradigm says its online service documentation and billing platform, Student Health Network (SHN), was not impacted.
Paradigm’s notification letters are dated September 14, 2026, roughly 11 months after the intrusion was detected. “We have no evidence that any of your information has been used to commit fraud or identity theft as a result of this incident,” the company said.
The notice doesn’t name the threat actor, explain how the attackers gained access, or say whether data was exfiltrated. Paradigm says it took certain systems offline, notified law enforcement, and brought in outside incident response experts.

articles.title: Most AI incident tools still leave a key decision to humans
articles.summary:
Most AI incident tools still leave a key decision to humans
An AI SRE agent can help troubleshoot an incident. But can you trust it to decide on its own when something needs attention?
Most teams treat agent autonomy as a yes or no question. For incident response, it is a progression with three phases, and many agents in production sit earlier on it than the teams running them realize. Most AI SRE tools still stop short of the final phase.
On Thursday, October 22, The New Stack hosts a live webinar with Raaz Dwivedi, co-founder and CTO of Traversal and an assistant professor at Cornell Tech. His team applies causal AI and agentic reasoning to production incidents. He will walk through where the industry sits on that progression and what it takes to move up.
You have successfully registered for the webinar.
The three phases of agent autonomy
Invoked: copilots, chat interfaces, and CLIs that wait for an on-call engineer to open them and ask a question mid-incident.
Background: scheduled jobs, alert rules, and triggers that fire on conditions someone predicted in advance.
Proactive: agents that decide for themselves when an incident needs attention, without waiting to be invoked or scheduled.
The first two phases share a limit. Each depends on a person noticing that something is wrong, or on someone predicting the right condition ahead of time. Proactive agents remove that dependency.

In the first post in this series, we built a semantic layer on AWS using Stardog’s knowledge graph over Amazon Aurora and Amazon Redshift and ran a Strands agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore against that layer. Stardog’s semantic layer is ontology-based: concepts and relationships modeled as RDF, with IRIs as the unit of federation and SPARQL as the query language. El problema era que esos datos quedaban sepultados bajo millones de anotaciones que ningún equipo de investigación podía revisar de forma manual.

Documentar esas dinámicas en el campo exige vigilancia continua, algo que ningún grupo de científicos puede sostener las 24 horas del día en cada rincón de un ecosistema. Sin embargo, cientos de millones de aficionados a la naturaleza ya lo hacían sin saberlo cada vez que anotaban lo observado en una plataforma digital.
Un equipo liderado por la Universidad de Míchigan demostró que la inteligencia artificial puede extraer y clasificar datos ecológicos ocultos en esos comentarios. Los resultados, divulgados en la revista Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, revelaron además indicios de especies vegetales foráneas en ecosistemas de la costa oeste de Estados Unidos, un tipo de alerta temprana que, sin este método, habría pasado inadvertida.

articles.title: Nebraska native explores galaxies far, far away
articles.summary:
Nebraska native explores galaxies far, far away
Megan Donahue ’85
Growing up on a small farm in Nebraska, Megan Donahue ’85 discovered the wider world by reading her way through her local library. Today, she is learning how the wider universe works by studying galaxy clusters.
Donahue discovered her passion for physics in that library at age 12 and started her path into astronomy thanks to “a providential interaction.” Through MIT’s Undergraduate Research Opportunities Program, she got introduced to cutting-edge x-ray imaging—work she found “really cool.”
Now a professor of physics and astronomy at Michigan State University, she researches galaxy clusters and baryonic matter (matter made of protons and neutrons, as opposed to dark matter) in an effort to learn more about the composition of the universe and its evolution.
“Clusters of galaxies are very large scoops of the universe,” says Donahue, who served as president of the American Astronomical Society from 2018 to 2020. “It’s like taking a sample from the ocean. If you’re trying to find out the average composition of the ocean’s water, you’d want to study as big a scoop as possible.”

According to the company, best known for major financial publications, including The Nikkei and Financial Times, the incident involved a cloud service it uses for system development.
On the morning of October 7, the hackers used previously compromised credentials to access the cloud service, Nikkei says.
While a total of 1.83 million records were stolen, about 1.68 million included only information that cannot be used to identify an individual, the company says.
Of the remaining records, 150,000 contained names, addresses, email addresses, phone numbers, and dates of birth, and 120,000 contained email addresses.
No credit card information was compromised in the attack, Nikkei says.
The media giant says it revoked the compromised credentials immediately after identifying the data breach and will take additional security measures if necessary.
It has notified regulators and continues to investigate the scope of the incident and the nature of the compromised data.
According to Nikkei, as of October 16, it has found no evidence that the stolen personal information has been misused.
The company also notes that the incident did not result in disruptions or data tampering.
“We deeply apologize for any inconvenience and concern this may have caused to those involved. We will inform you individually if the leakage of personal information is confirmed,” Nikkei said.

articles.title: A good TA: priceless
articles.summary:
A good TA: priceless
Tom Davis ’84, SM ’85
These are images of quizzes I took in 3.091, Introduction to Solid-State Chemistry, in the fall of 1980.
One is my very first exam at MIT, and getting 49 out of 100 was a soul-crushing experience. I can still picture the TA, Leszek Pawlowicz, PhD ’87, returning my paper. He had a big smile on his face, and he said something to the effect of “I expect to see you double your score on the next quiz!”
Well, I got the message. Studying at MIT was not like studying in high school, but I got 100 on the next quiz and graduated with good enough grades to get me into grad school. All it took, it seems, was that initial kick in the seat of my pants, then a kind hand helping me up off the ground.
Recently, I connected with Leszek, and he replied with a charming note. It felt good to let him know how much his encouragement meant to me. A good TA can really have lasting impact!

A Nvidia consolidou sua presença nesse mercado ao longo de anos de investimentos no CUDA, sua plataforma de software que permite executar aplicações de IA em seus processadores gráficos. Como consequência, boa parte dos programas desenvolvidos com PyTorch já está adaptada para funcionar com o hardware da companhia. She warned that frontier models are trained to get results and aren’t built around organizational norms or judgment. “These agents are frequently overprivileged, have access to data, tools and systems and can take actions and make decisions in critical processes,” Gallot wrote.
Nadim Abdo, Microsoft’s corporate vice president of identity and network access, clarified the insider label. “This does not mean agents are inherently malicious. articles.title: AI’s Midas problem: When code is free, features are worthless
articles.summary:
AI’s Midas problem: When code is free, features are worthless
Every team that adopted Claude Code, Cursor, or Copilot to produce more code has the same problem: When output is free, offering volume stops being a viable strategy. In fact, teams accelerating their software development with AI may be giving up the very thing that makes their software valuable.
It’s time to remember what makes software valuable and why racing to produce a mountain of code and features leads to failure.
The Midas touch
In Ovid’s tale, Midas, king of Phrygia, took in the missing satyr Silenus, whom Phrygian peasants had found drunk, granted him ten days of hospitality, and then returned him to Dionysus. In return, he was offered the reward of his choice: whatever he wished for. Famously, he wished that everything he touched would turn to gold.
Testing his new ability on an oak twig and then a stone, Midas was delighted. Nathaniel Hawthorne, who retold the myth for children in 1851, added a rose garden: His Midas turns every bloom to gold, still delighted, though his daughter Marygold mourns that the roses no longer smell sweet. In both versions, the celebration ends at the table, where food and drink turn to gold in his hands. That’s when Midas realized his reward was a bane, not a blessing, and asked to be rid of it.
Many leaders who force-fed AI to developers are now coming to a realization similar to that of Midas.

Artificial Intelligence

Agentic AI applications need governed access to live enterprise data. That data can live in operational systems, analytical warehouses, SaaS applications, other clouds, or on premises. In the previous post in this series, we built a semantic layer on AWS using Stardog’s knowledge graph over Amazon Aurora and Amazon Redshift. A Strands agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore queried that layer. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. This post uses the same customer 360 pattern, but swaps in a different semantic layer implementation and extends the source mix.
Two things change here. First, the semantic layer is the Denodo Platform: an AI data layer that provides active context and live, zero-copy access to distributed enterprise data. The agent talks to it in VQL, Denodo’s SQL dialect. Second, the source mix includes an on-premises PostgreSQL database alongside Amazon Aurora and Amazon Redshift, so the federation problem is no longer bounded by an Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC).
The rest of the pattern carries over. A foundation model on Amazon Bedrock plans and writes queries. The Denodo MCP Server exposes governed views to the agent through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). articles.title: Hackers explotan una falla en Plex para instalar mineros de criptomonedas en miles de servidores
articles.summary:
Piratas informáticos explotan desde el 17 de octubre una cadena de cuatro fallas de seguridad en Plex Media Server para tomar control remoto de servidores domésticos sin necesitar contraseña, instalar mineros de criptomonedas y convertir los equipos en intermediarios de tráfico anónimo.
La cadena de fallas, bautizada Plex2Shell, combina cuatro vulnerabilidades: un fraude de solicitudes del lado del servidor sin autenticación, acceso indebido a funciones internas del programa, robo del token de administrador del dueño del servidor y escritura arbitraria de archivos en la carpeta de códecs. Combinadas, permiten ejecutar código con los mismos permisos que el propio servicio de Plex.
Plex corrigió las cuatro fallas a comienzos de septiembre con la versión 1.43.3 y pidió entonces a los usuarios que actualizaran. Tres semanas después publicó los identificadores correspondientes: CVE-2026-96652, CVE-2026-96654, CVE-2026-96655 y CVE-2026-96656, una de ellas con una gravedad de 8,6 sobre 10.
Un investigador de seguridad publicó el 16 de octubre un informe técnico con el código capaz de encadenar las cuatro fallas y ejecutarlas de forma remota sin necesidad de credenciales válidas.
“Estas vulnerabilidades están siendo explotadas de manera activa y generalizada. Si su servidor es anterior a la versión 1.43.3.10861 y es accesible desde internet, asuma que puede estar comprometido”, advirtió Plex en un comunicado publicado el 19 de octubre en su foro oficial de soporte.

articles.summary:
Neuf ans après le fiasco des lootbox de Battlefront II, qui avait poussé Disney à intervenir en coulisses auprès d’EA, l’engouement du public pour le jeu n’a paradoxalement jamais faibli. D’après EGM, les dirigeants de Lucasfilm déploient « activement des droïdes sondes » pour trouver un studio partenaire capable de relancer la série sans rejouer le fiasco de 2017. DICE et Bungie seraient dans le collimateur.
Le retour de DICE pour Star Wars Battlefront 3 ?
Le nom de DICE n’a rien d’une surprise : le studio suédois a développé les deux Battlefront d’EA, en 2015 et 2017, et maîtrise le moteur Frostbite comme les grandes batailles multijoueur. Celui de Bungie est beaucoup plus inattendu. Racheté par Sony en 2022, le studio connaît déjà Lucasfilm : les deux entreprises ont travaillé ensemble sur Destiny 2: Renegades, une extension inspirée de Star Wars, avec sabres laser et blasters, sortie le 2 décembre 2025. EGM ne dit pas si cette collaboration a pesé dans la balance.
Pour Lucasfilm, chaque option a ses atouts et ses risques. L’option DICE représente la facilité technique et la sécurité des ressources graphiques déjà existantes, à condition que le studio ait retenu les leçons du passé et ne soit pas totalement essoré par le développement de ses propres franchises.

articles.title: Building Physical AI Systems That Can Work in the Real World - EE Times
articles.summary:
Physical AI brings AI into machines that must sense their surroundings, make decisions, and act in the physical world. The market opportunity is substantial: McKinsey estimates that AI-powered agents and robots could unlock about $2.9 trillion in annual economic value in the U.S. by 2030. However, realizing this opportunity depends on moving from working prototypes to products that can operate reliably, safely, and economically at scale.
That exposes a different engineering problem. In a prototype, teams can often add more compute, sensors, cooling, or power to prove that a capability works. In deployment, every added capability must fit within the size, weight, power, and cost budget, often abbreviated to SWaP-C, of the system.
Those constraints shape how a robot performs: How long it can operate between charges, how much productive payload it can carry, and how reliably it operates over time. The challenge is not simply adding more intelligence but integrating it effectively into deployable products.
A robot must continuously interpret its surroundings, decide how to respond, and translate those decisions into physical action. Doing that requires capabilities from perception and AI inference to planning and motion control to work together, while meeting different compute and timing requirements.

Beam is a new Mac app that takes a window running on one Mac and puts it on another, where it behaves like a locally installed app. Why? Agents.
Serial founder Hiten Shah, who co-founded Crazy Egg and KISSmetrics, built it with Sam Asante under a company called Noats. It launched on Product Hunt on Tuesday and is aimed at the headless Mac Mini sitting in a closet running AI agents.
The pitch is great: Instead of opening Screen Sharing and steering a full remote desktop, a user picks a single window on the other machine, say a Terminal session or a browser window an agent is working in, and it opens alongside everything else on the Mac in front of them. It gets its own Dock icon and can be called using the Command+Tab switcher. Resizing the window resizes the window on the other Mac. Keyboard shortcuts work, files can be dragged across, and the app’s audio can play locally. The app itself never leaves the original machine. When one window isn’t enough, Beam can pull over a full display or the whole Mac.
Shah frames it around his own setup in his Product Hunt launch post, describing Macs running agents and local models “with work continuing even when nobody’s sitting in front of them.” Getting to one of those machines usually means Screen Sharing and a second desktop to navigate. Beam is meant to cut that down to the one window that matters.

Now he is applying his management expertise as CEO of Costa Pickleball, a Las Vegas–based startup that sells high-performance paddles in decorative designs. Succeeding in today’s pickleball market will be tough, but Anderson thinks he has what it takes, partly thanks to an important lesson he learned at MIT: “There’s nothing you can’t accomplish if you are willing to put effort into it.”

articles.title: Spectrum costs squeeze African telecom investment and growth
articles.summary:
Africa’s mobile networks have expanded significantly over the past decade, bringing coverage to more people. But wider coverage has not translated into widespread internet use or network quality on par with other regions.
A new report by the GSMA, Spectrum Policy in Africa: Enabling Investment and Empowering Consumers Through Effective Spectrum Pricing, identifies the high cost of accessing radio spectrum—the invisible radio frequencies that carry mobile calls and internet data—as a central bottleneck. African mobile operators pay significantly more for relatively less spectrum, leaving them with limited capacity to expand or improve service quality.
According to GSMA Intelligence, spectrum costs consume 0.82% of mobile operators’ revenue per 100 MHz in Africa, compared with 0.66% in the rest of the world. Meanwhile, African operators hold an average of about 570 MHz of spectrum below 7 GHz, 24% less than the global peer average of approximately 750 MHz.
The imbalance extends beyond price and availability to licence duration. Only nine African countries routinely grant spectrum licences lasting 20 years or more, while licences of 20 years or indefinite duration are standard across Europe, North America and developed Asian markets.
Lowering spectrum fees could free up vital capital for network expansion, but lower fees alone do not guarantee better connectivity. The crucial test for African regulators is whether more affordable access can be tied to measurable improvements in …

Derzeit tobt ein Preiskampf um die Konditionen für die neue private Rentenvorsorge. Das Altersvorsorgedepot ist als Nachfolger der Riester-Rente geplant und soll Anfang 2027 starten. Der Staat steuert dann bis zu 540 Euro jährlich bei, wenn Sparer über Fonds, ETFs oder Anleihen fürs Alter vorsorgen.
Anbieter eines geförderten Altersvorsorgedepots müssen ein sogenanntes Standarddepot bereitstellen, bei dem die Effektivkosten maximal ein Prozent betragen dürfen. Das Geld wird dabei nach gesetzlichen Vorgaben auf einen Aktien- und einen Anleihen-Fonds verteilt.

Each task in Cairn is considered a project, with an origin and a predefined goal, and agents work step by step from origin to goal, posting their intents and findings to a shared blackboard.
Following a recent Gambit Security report on hackers using three AI harnesses to automate attacks against hundreds of online retailers, Norforge decided to investigate further and discovered that some threat actors left their panels open.
On Cairn, the cybersecurity firm identified three clusters of activity that appear to be malicious, focused on persistent access and financial theft.

articles.title: Robotic therapy for stroke patients

Robotic therapy for stroke patients
An adaptive physical rehab system uses generative AI to learn from physical therapists and offer personalized support.
Strokes leave 5 million people with long-term impairments each year, and a growing shortage of physical therapists makes it hard for them to get the care they need. A new approach tries to solve that problem by combining artificial intelligence and human therapy.
Johannes Lachner, a former MIT postdoc who is now an assistant professor at Purdue University, and Noah Geiger, a former visiting student at MIT, developed a robotic system that uses generative AI and real-time force feedback to learn from real therapists. Drawing on what it’s learned, it gives patients just the right amount of assistance during physical rehabilitation exercises like reaching, lifting their arms, and performing tasks of daily living.
The goal is “not to replace therapists, but to extend their reach,” Lachner says.
“Initial robotic experiments have already demonstrated the feasibility of this approach,” he reports. “The next phase of the project aims to develop therapist-specific models and evaluate them in a long-term clinical study with the same patients who previously received manual therapy.” Beyond that, he envisions possible applications in contact-rich industrial settings or collaborative workspaces.

AI review took over bug-finding. But it didn’t take over the conversation where a team debates what it decided and why, and that is the part I missed too.
The part AI review doesn’t solve
Most teams are stuck in one of two modes. They review every line and become the bottleneck, or they rubber-stamp and lose track of what changed and why. There is no middle ground yet.
“The argument over whether engineers should stop reading code is over, because we already have.”
AI review is good at the mechanical half of the job. It never gets tired, it reads every line, and it holds the same standard on every PR. But it never saw what was decided. It won’t tell you not to build something, and it can’t be accountable for the result. A better model won’t fix that, because the tool reads the wrong artifact at the wrong time.
As I wrote in “Kill the code review theater, keep the review,” code review is how a team builds a mental model of its system. That has been the only scheduled moment for engineers to talk to each other about that system. Teams that hand code reviews to AI tools rarely notice they’ve also given up that moment.

Artificial Intelligence
Securing AI agent identity with X.509 PKI on AWS
When AI agents access databases, APIs, and sensitive business operations, establishing cryptographic identity through X.509 public key infrastructure (PKI) becomes a critical requirement. The core challenge is proving which agent made a request, preventing forgery between agents, and confirming that each agent acts only on behalf of an authorized user. Traditional approaches such as sharing API keys between components or passing OAuth tokens through agent chains fall short of the zero-trust requirements that enterprise deployments demand.
Multi-agent AI frameworks increasingly use the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to connect agents to external tools and data sources. MCP defines how a large language model (LLM)-powered agent invokes tools such as database queries or email operations. However, MCP has no built-in authentication standard. It is transport-agnostic by design. This creates a critical gap: Without proper identity mechanisms, any component could impersonate an agent, replay intercepted credentials, or invoke tools without authorization.
In this post, we show you how to address this gap using Keyfactor EJBCA combined with AWS services. EJBCA is a PKI platform that supports high-availability deployment, REST API automation, and Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) validation. Nigeria’s telecom regulator launched a device verification tool that lets buyers check whether a phone is approved for use on local mobile networks. But enforcing compliance across an import-dependent market could test the agency’s technical reach.
With 99% of smartphones imported into Nigeria and an estimated 63 million mobile devices sold annually, the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) faces a market structured around multi-layered supply chains, informal distribution networks, and varied entry routes.
Launched on October 7, 2026, the NCC’s Device Checker requires consumers to dial *315# to verify whether a phone meets Type Approval requirements—the NCC’s mandatory regulation that all communication equipment must meet before connecting to local networks.
The regulator says the tool is part of a broader effort to enforce its Device Management System (DMS) under Section 132(2) of the Nigerian Communications Act 2003.
The checker uses a phone’s International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI), a unique 15-digit identifier, to verify its status against the NCC’s approved equipment records. By linking device records to import declarations, the regulator says it can investigate whether a phone was properly declared to the Nigeria Customs Service and trace the business responsible for importing it.

After coding agents spit out new code, it still needs testing, and traditionally that meant humans writing the tests. That work includes deciding which user flows need testing, scripting tests for them, and rejiggering them when those flows change.

articles.title: A reason to eat carbs
articles.summary:
A reason to eat carbs
MIT researchers have found that a ketogenic diet may fuel the growth of some intestinal tumors.
A high-fat, low-carbohydrate diet can help some people lose weight, and some research has shown that it may protect against colon cancer. But a new study suggests that such a ketogenic diet may also increase the risk of cancer in the small intestine.
This type of diet forces the body to burn fatty acids instead of carbohydrates for fuel, producing by-products called ketone bodies. One of these, BHB, was thought to be responsible for the protective effect observed against colon cancer.
Omer Yilmaz, director of the MIT Stem Cell Initiative, worked with colleagues including MIT postdocs Jessica Shay and Fangtao Chi to investigate whether the effects were similar in the small intestine. But instead, they found that mice on a ketogenic diet were more likely to develop tumors in that part of the gastrointestinal system than those on a control diet were.
Additional studies revealed that this tumor growth was driven by the way intestinal cells burn dietary fat for energy—a metabolic pathway called fatty acid oxidation. This pathway activates proteins that signal stem cells to multiply more rapidly.
“Having more stem cells means that when you injure the small intestine, it can repair itself better, but the downside is that having more active stem cells can lead to tumor formation,” Yilmaz says.

articles.title: À 10 mètres sous l'eau, ces panneaux solaires ont réussi à recharger une batterie — Frandroid
articles.summary:
La lumière du soleil reste exploitable sous l’eau, même à 10 mètres de profondeur. C’est ce qu’ont montré des chercheurs de l’université du Yunnan, en Chine, associés notamment à l’EPFL de Lausanne, lors d’une expérience menée en conditions réelles en mer de Chine méridionale. Avec des cellules photovoltaïques immergées, ils ont produit assez d’électricité pour charger une batterie, qui a ensuite alimenté un panneau LED. Leurs travaux ont été publiés le 11 septembre dans la revue Joule.
Une cellule photovoltaïque adaptée aux longueurs d’onde sous-marines
Les panneaux solaires classiques sont mal adaptés à une utilisation sous-marine. Sous l’eau, le rouge et l’infrarouge sont vite absorbés, si bien que ces panneaux perdent une bonne partie de la lumière dont ils se servent sur terre. Pour tenir compte de ces conditions, les chercheurs ont développé une cellule photovoltaïque à base de pérovskite aux halogénures de plomb. Celle-ci convertit surtout la lumière bleue et verte, celle qui pénètre le plus loin dans l’eau, et son absorption est calée sur la lumière qui reste à 10 mètres de profondeur.
Les scientifiques ont également intégré à la pérovskite un polymère appelé chlorhydrate de polyhexaméthylène guanidine. Cet additif corrige des défauts du matériau et limite la migration des ions, ce qui améliore les performances de la cellule et sa stabilité dans le temps.

The acquisition of Berlin-based Talon.One by Dutch payments provider Adyen in July 2026 offers a useful perspective on European technology investing. A company founded in Germany developed technology valuable to a global payments business, and its next chapter is being written within Europe. This is a significant outcome for the founders and investors. However, it also raises a larger question: how can Europe turn individual successes into an ecosystem capable of producing them repeatedly?
The answer is not simply to encourage more European acquisitions. Successful startups need access to the best opportunities available, whether their future lies with a European buyer, an international technology group or the public markets. What matters is that these decisions reflect commercial potential rather than a lack of viable alternatives. For Europe, the challenge is to create the conditions in which successful companies can scale, attract investment and generate lasting economic value.

articles.title: Data centre vs Cloud platform: Is there a difference?
articles.summary:
You have probably seen the words “data centre” and “cloud” used interchangeably. They don’t mean the same thing, and the difference matters. It shapes how businesses buy technology, how regulators write rules and where investors see opportunity.
A data centre is a building. It is a secure, purpose-built facility with reliable power, cooling, security and internet connections, so that computers can run around the clock. A cloud platform is a service. It is software that lets customers rent computing power, storage, and networking on demand, switch them on or off themselves, and pay only for what they use.
Think of an airport and an airline. The airport provides the runway, fuel, and terminal; the airline provides the service you actually book. Every cloud platform runs inside a data centre, but most data centres do not offer a cloud platform. Owning an airport does not make you an airline.
Data centre grading and cloud computing standards
Companies that rent space for their own servers in someone else’s facility are buying what the industry calls “colocation”. A facility’s reliability is rated on a four-level scale from the Uptime Institute.
Tier I has no backup equipment, so any fault results in downtime. Tier II adds spares but has a single path for power and cooling.
Tier III has more than one path, so any part can be serviced without switching anything off; it is the level most serious operators aim for. Tier IV survives any single failure.

articles.title: Melt it, spin it, use it again
articles.summary:
Melt it, spin it, use it again
A plastic-based recyclable yarn is as strong and stretchy as spandex.
The average American throws out around 81 pounds of clothing each year, and there are few options for recycling it. MIT engineers hope to cut down on that textile waste with a new type of yarn.
The thermoplastic yarn mimics the properties of conventional elastic yarns, which typically combine spandex with polyester or nylon. Those fibers would have to be separated for recycling—a process that isn’t practical. But the MIT team found a way to create a similarly stretchy yarn from two variations of polyethylene, a material commonly used in milk jugs and grocery bags. Because they come from the same chemical family, the yarn can be melted as is. Svetlana Boriskina, who led the work as a research scientist in the Department of Mechanical Engineering, says a garment made from this material could then be spun into new yarn for a next generation of clothing. Even after 10 cycles of melting and respinning, the yarn stays as strong and flexible as conventional thread.
“Now we have something that can be knitted and woven,” Boriskina says. “That is the next stage.” Someday, the researchers hope, a polyethylene garment could be dropped in a collection bin and sent to a recycling facility, promoting a more sustainable, circular textile economy.

Cross-Region inference is a capacity mechanism. Your application calls the Amazon Bedrock Runtime endpoint in your source Region. articles.title: Here’s the tea
articles.summary:
Here’s the tea
An MIT historian uncovers the true origins of an artifact once thought to be a relic of the Boston Tea Party.
When Tristan Brown, an associate professor of history at MIT, first examined a Chinese tea chest label displayed at Old South Meeting House, he had no reason to doubt its story. Descendants of the Boston blacksmith Thomas Wells had donated the label in 1987, saying it had been recovered after colonial protesters threw tea into Boston Harbor in 1773.
But after a year of research, Brown reached a different conclusion: The label was made nearly a century later. The decisive clue came when he read the Chinese text in Cantonese rather than Mandarin, as previous scholars had done. He found that the characters had been used phonetically, in slightly variant forms across contemporary sources, to represent the name of Smith, Archer & Co., a US firm that acquired Asian tea for shipment to American markets during the 1860s and 1870s.
Working with the Wells family, he traced the label to a relative who traveled from Michigan to California during the Gold Rush era before returning and operating a business known as the California Tea Store. Brown argues that claims for its revolutionary pedigree probably developed later, amid the centennial commemorations of the 1870s.
The discovery does not make the label historically insignificant, he says. Instead, what began as an inquiry into a supposed artifact of the Boston Tea Party became a study of how ordinary objects acqu…

articles.title: AOMEI Backupper Compromised in Short-Burst Supply Chain Campaign

AOMEI Backupper is Windows backup, sync, and disk cloning software, available in free and paid editions for home users, businesses, and Windows Server environments. AOMEI says its products are used by more than 186 million people worldwide.
Unlike typical supply chain attacks, this campaign relied on short-lived tampering windows to serve the CrossRoad downloader and the ShinyRoad backdoor.
“Each tampering window remained active for only five to ten minutes before reverting to authentic versions,” report Google Cloud’s Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant, which investigated the attack alongside ManageEngine Threat Analysis Lab (METAL).

Le ministre Markwayne Mullin a signé l’ordre le 24 juillet, mais il n’a été rendu public que ce lundi 19 octobre, selon Reuters. Il a suivi une recommandation du Federal Acquisition Security Council, le comité chargé d’évaluer ces risques. L’ordre, publié ce mardi au Federal Register (le journal officiel américain), s’impose donc aux agences. Elles peuvent quand même demander des exceptions.

articles.title: Assess the entire inference stack — not just open model benchmarks
articles.summary:
Assess the entire inference stack — not just open model benchmarks
Impressive benchmark results should make it easy for engineers to select the right open model for the outcome they are tasked with developing. However, that is not the case.
Benchmarks indicate an open model’s optimal performance, but in production, a model must work repeatedly. The challenge is that in production, other factors matter, such as the information provided to the model and its accuracy. So benchmarks can’t tell an engineer whether the AI they are developing will complete the task accurately, or even at all. This is especially important for long-horizon AI tasks.
Ryan Hanrui Wang, SVP of Applied AI at AI cloud provider Nebius, tells The New Stack it is important to measure an open model by the industry benchmarks in conjunction with internal benchmarks and harnesses to ensure you get the inference outcomes the organization requires, something he says the Amsterdam, Netherlands-based company always does in partnership with its clients.
Wang joined Nebius when it acquired Eigen AI, the inference-optimization startup he co-founded and led as CEO, in a roughly $643 million deal announced in May; Nebius sells inference through its Token Factory platform.
“Customers often have their own benchmarks, so we can use their agent workflow and its traces to see the level of success we can work with. We always work closely with them to define the benchmarks.”

It’s a bird, it’s a plane … it’s a robo-puffin?
MIT engineers’ design for a robot that both swims and flies could lead to a new class of vehicles for ocean exploration.
Given that water is 1,000 times denser than air, moving through those two mediums requires very different mechanics—or so one might assume. Yet birds like gulls and puffins can plunge into the sea, swim underwater, and leap back into the air to fly away. And now engineers at MIT and EPFL in Lausanne, Switzerland, have designed a robot that can do likewise.
The “flapping-wing aerial-aquatic vehicle,” or FAAV, weighs less than 300 grams (about half a pound) and is equipped with a central fuselage, two flexible wings, and a steerable tail. The body contains a battery and a waterproof electric motor that drives a crankshaft, which pumps the wings up and down at preset frequencies. The wings are made of thin membranes that are coated with hydrophobic nanoparticles to help wick away water. And the tail is motorized, enabling it to change its angle to help the robot fly up or dive down.
In experiments carried out in a water tank and at Lake Geneva, a team led by Raphael Zufferey, an assistant professor of mechanical engineering at MIT, identified combinations of wing size, flapping frequency, and tail angle that enable the robot to smoothly transition from swimming to flying.

articles.title: Fine-tuning GPT-OSS-20B for multilingual reasoning on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Fine-tuning GPT-OSS-20B for multilingual reasoning on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
GPT-OSS-20B is an open-weight reasoning model that thinks in English. Ask it to reason in French, German, Spanish, or Italian and it acknowledges the instruction, then produces its chain-of-thought in English anyway. On a 50-example multilingual reasoning test, the base model reasoned in the correct target language only 22 percent of the time. That 22 percent was almost entirely the English examples (English 100 percent, French 0 percent, German 10 percent, Spanish 0 percent, Italian 0 percent).
For teams deploying reasoning models for non-English users, that gap matters. A user who asks a question in French expects the model to reason and answer in French, not to switch to English mid-thought. Closing that gap is a fine-tuning problem. It raises a question every team faces once they start customizing open-weight models: supervised fine-tuning (SFT), reinforcement learning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), or both?
In this post, we walk through how we fine-tuned GPT-OSS-20B for multilingual reasoning on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod. We show when SFT alone was sufficient and when GRPO added measurable value on top. To understand more broadly when GRPO helps, we also ran a controlled Qwen2.5-7B experiment across two tasks with different capability gaps. The report (Key Practices for Incident Readiness and Response in Super Intelligence Training and Evaluation) uses the term super intelligence (SI) rather than artificial intelligence (AI) in line with presidential executive order 14434.
In the report, the ten key practices are grouped into five stages: prepare, detect, respond, recover, and report. For clarity, the report also includes three useful terminology definitions covering AI agents, AI control incident, and AI control near-miss.

articles.title: Meta Muse exposes users' personal and business secrets when they share conversations
articles.summary:
Muse, the new general-purpose AI agent from Meta, can expose sensitive information when users share conversations through web links, researchers reported Monday. In response to questions from Ars about the behavior, Meta said it’s suspending the sharing feature while the company reviews it and considers making changes.
Like many online services, Muse has allowed users to share searches, conversations, images, and similar content with other people. Such share features usually involve clicking an option to create a unique URL that anyone can use to load a page hosting the content. To keep potentially sensitive information from being accessible to unintended people, the URLs typically contain a long sequence of text that can’t be easily guessed.
A single query is all that’s required
Muse, which Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said last month was “built from the ground up for privacy and security,” seems to take the same precautions. But a central design decision for constructing URLs has made the links easy to discover. As a result, researchers from security firm Claroc said they were able to enumerate 6,800 links Muse users created for sharing conversations with others. After opening a few hundred of them, the researchers found information that was clearly not intended to be publicly available, including:

Taking to X, Cloudflare’s director of engineering Christoph Nakazawa confirmed that the company is taking ownership of tsrs, a Rust port of TypeScript that it claims is up to eight times faster, and uses 70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0.
Microsoft’s own TypeScript compiler is reaping the benefits, too, with the teams sharing optimizations as they work to keep the two implementations in sync.
“We are not forking TypeScript — we are working with the TypeScript team and as a result 7.1 is already ~2.5x faster, too,” Nakazawa writes.
That “port vs fork” message runs throughout the accompanying blog post, co-authored by Nakazawa and fellow Cloudflare engineers Boshen Chen and Dimitri Mitropoulos, who go to great lengths to explain that they very much see TypeScript as Microsoft’s to continue steering.
“To be clear, we are not forking TypeScript. We believe the TypeScript team should remain in full control of the language’s design and direction.”

articles.title: Windows Server 2025 gets support for quick machine recovery
articles.summary:
Microsoft announced that IT administrators can now use quick machine recovery on Windows Server 2025 after installing the October 2026 security update.
Quick machine recovery (QMR) lets IT admins fix critical boot failures with targeted Windows Update fixes without physical access to affected systems.
When enabled, it boots into the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) and launches the QMR Tool if Windows 11 fails to start because of a configuration change or a new driver. It then sends crash data to Microsoft, which can remotely fix issues by adjusting settings or removing problematic drivers or updates.
"With the October 2026 security update, quick machine recovery extends to Windows Server 2025," the company said in a message center update.
"Quick machine recovery is designed to help restore devices experiencing widespread boot issues by using the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) to search Windows Update for applicable remediations."
On Windows Server 2025, cloud remediation is disabled by default, but admins can enable it via Group Policy under Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Quick Machine Recovery to retrieve and apply cloud-sourced remediation.
For local configuration, admins must sign in to the target server with administrator permissions and use the Local Group Policy Editor. Meta’s AI companion, Muse, is now one of only a dozen mobile apps to have reached 10 million U.S. downloads in its first 40 days on the market. According to new data from market intelligence provider Sensor Tower, Muse has seen 10.9 million downloads since its September debut, 10.2 million of which were in the United States.
Only 11 other apps to date have reached this type of post-launch milestone, said Sensor Tower’s Senior Insights Analyst Kara Lee. The most recent of these was Meta’s Threads, back in July 2023.
Other apps that saw this kind of scale were largely mobile games, Lee noted, like Fortnite, PUBG Mobile, Pokémon GO, and others. Besides Threads, Disney+ was the only other non-game app to make it into the exclusive club.

Respan spent two years building on LiteLLM. One upgrade made it start over.
Respan released an open-source AI gateway written in Rust on Tuesday, after spending two years building more than 100,000 lines of wrapper code around LiteLLM.
The new gateway replaces that system with a small core and plugins that handle model providers, routing, MCP tools, realtime voice, and security controls.
A LiteLLM upgrade breaks
The breaking point came in January 2026, when a routine LiteLLM upgrade caused intermittent connection failures. Respan rolled back the update but never figured out the problem.
“We still haven’t figured out the cause,” the company said in its Hacker News launch post.
Since then, its engineers have stopped upgrading LiteLLM directly, instead pulling in upstream fixes one at a time.
A small plugin core
To avoid another maintenance headache, the company borrowed an idea from Nginx, keeping the gateway’s core small and moving features like routing, model providers, and security into plugins. Developers can build their own using the same interfaces, without having to change the underlying code.

articles.title: Beyond the KV cache: Training and serving i14’s Laplace 3B linear attention model on AWS Trainium2 with native PyTorch | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Beyond the KV cache: Training and serving i14’s Laplace 3B linear attention model on AWS Trainium2 with native PyTorch
Most large language models (LLMs) use transformer architectures with softmax attention. During inference, their key-value (KV) cache grows with the conversation or document context. This can reduce concurrency, increase serving cost, and force agentic applications to discard useful history.
i14 designed Laplace 3B as a linear attention alternative. Its recurrent state stays at 29.5 MB per sequence, independent of context length. Working with AWS, i14 used native PyTorch support through TorchNeuron Native to bring this custom architecture to AWS Trainium2. This preserved its Gated Linear Attention (GLA) design and Muon optimizer.
On one trn2.48xlarge instance, Laplace 3B trained at about 120,000 tokens per second. The model served 11,544 output tokens per second across 1,280 concurrent sequences. This post explains the model design, the changes i14 made for Trainium2, and the training and inference results.
About i14
i14 is an AI research and technology company that develops model architectures, components, and runtimes. Its work draws on AI, computational cognitive science, and research into how biological systems learn over time. i14 applies these ideas to models that can retain long-range context without allowing serving state to grow with every token.

articles.title: Polestar tries to quantify what it’s like to drive a performance car
articles.summary:
The human desire to go fast is old, dating back at least as far as the first time some adventurous Yamnaya saw a horse on the Pontic-Caspian steppe and thought, “I bet if I jumped on that thing’s back, it would be faster than walking.”
A thousand years later, someone else invented the wheel—and the chariot—and humanity was ready to roll. Now, about five millennia since that first horseback ride, equestrianism is mostly a leisure activity, and we drive cars, propelled by motors with more power than an entire herd of beasts could muster.
Acceleration, top speed, and lap times are the usual ways we quantify that performance, and performance electric vehicles are currently in an arms race to see which one can hit 60 mph in the least amount of time. But measuring a car’s performance is easy—all you need is a stopwatch and a track. How about measuring the effect of car performance on the driver? That’s a question Polestar is trying to answer with researchers at the University of Oxford.
“As electric cars redefine what performance can be, we wanted to understand something that can’t be captured by a specification sheet alone: the human experience behind the wheel,” said Christian Samson, Polestar’s head of product attributes. “Working with University of Oxford allows us to look at performance through a different lens—connecting the engineering of the car with the experience of the person driving it.”

L'objectif de cet outil pédagogique est donc d'apporter "une information complémentaire aux citoyens et aux collectivités", mais aussi "d’orienter la surveillance vers les zones où l’exposition est susceptible d’être plus élevée." articles.title: CJIS v6.1 Compliance: 5 Practical Priorities for Agencies

For agencies responsible for protecting Criminal Justice Information (CJI), meeting CJIS requirements means more than putting security controls in place. Those controls need to work across the systems staff use every day, and agencies need to be able to prove they're effective.
But, between legacy systems, stretched IT teams, and constantly changing access needs, even agencies with strong security practices can struggle to apply controls consistently and keep the evidence auditors expect.
So, where should you focus your efforts? In this article, we'll walk through five key areas agencies should be paying attention to under CJIS v6.1, with practical advice to make compliance easier to manage.
Multi-Factor Authentication
CJIS v6.1 requires MFA for both privileged and non-privileged accounts under controls IA-2(1) and IA-2(2), covering local, network, and remote access. The challenge is making sure no accounts slip through the cracks.
Start by reviewing MFA coverage across your environment, paying particular attention to legacy applications and administrative accounts. When implementing MFA, consider phishing-resistant methods such as FIDO2 security keys.
You'll also need reliable processes for enrolling, replacing, and revoking authenticators.

Guillaume Lample, cofondateur et directeur scientifique de Mistral AI, a annoncé ce mardi 20 octobre sur X l’arrivée de Voxtral 3. Il présente cette famille de modèles vocaux comme « SOTA », l’état de l’art dans le jargon. Quelques mois après l’annonce de son grand modèle de langage Large 4, la start-up parisienne vend cette fois aux entreprises de quoi faire décrocher une IA au téléphone. Et elle peut tourner sur les serveurs du client, qui garde alors ses appels chez lui.
Sur sa page de présentation, Mistral publie ses prix et une série de graphiques comparatifs. Ses modèles de transcription couvrent plus de 50 langues, sa synthèse vocale plus de 35. En mars 2026, Voxtral TTS, son premier modèle de synthèse vocale, n’en gérait que 9.
Quatre briques pour faire parler une IA au téléphone
La transcription repose sur deux modèles, Voxtral Small Transcribe 3 et Voxtral Mini Transcribe 3, qui traitent des fichiers audio en différé. Ils savent séparer les voix (qui a dit quoi) et s’aider d’une liste de mots techniques fournie par le client. La version Mini coûte 0,0035 dollar la minute, soit environ 19 centimes d’euro HT pour une heure d’audio.
Pour le direct, Voxtral Mini Transcribe Realtime 3 transcrit en moins d’une demi-seconde dans plus de 35 langues. Il repère aussi le moment où l’interlocuteur a fini sa phrase, pour que l’agent ne lui coupe pas la parole.
