articles.title: Spotify : ce nouveau QR code pourrait sérieusement compliquer le partage de votre abonnement
articles.summary:
Spotify renforce la vérification des abonnements Premium Famille avec un QR code à scanner en présence du gestionnaire. Une procédure qui pourrait compliquer le partage entre plusieurs foyers, avec des conséquences importantes pour ceux qui ne respectent pas le délai imposé.
Partager son abonnement Spotify avec cinq proches, c’est pratique pour réduire la facture. Encore faut-il vivre sous le même toit, une condition que la plateforme impose depuis longtemps, mais dont la vérification reposait principalement sur une adresse postale. Spotify semble désormais décidé à aller plus loin. Certains utilisateurs doivent confirmer leur présence physique auprès du titulaire de l’abonnement en scannant un QR code sur son téléphone. Une manipulation assez simple en apparence, mais qui pourrait compliquer les arrangements entre amis ou membres d’une famille vivant à plusieurs adresses.
Un QR code à scanner en personne pour conserver son abonnement
Comme le rapporte 9to5Google, Spotify déploie une nouvelle procédure destinée à vérifier que les membres d’un abonnement Premium Famille résident bien avec le propriétaire du compte.
Le fonctionnement est détaillé dans la documentation officielle française de Spotify. Lorsqu’un membre reçoit une demande de vérification, le gestionnaire doit ouvrir l’application Spotify sur son téléphone, accéder à la rubrique « Votre abonnement Premium », puis sélectionner « Gérer » pour afficher un QR code.

articles.title: Dans les coulisses des tournages de Top Gun: Maverick et F1, l’épisode 3 de Color Matters est arrivé
articles.summary:
Dans les coulisses des tournages de Top Gun: Maverick et F1, l’épisode 3 de Color Matters est arrivé
Comment conserver des couleurs fidèles lorsque les images d’un film proviennent de dizaines de caméras différentes ? Le troisième épisode de Color Matters nous plonge dans les coulisses de Top Gun: Maverick, The Phoenician Scheme et F1, avec un spécialiste de l’image hollywoodienne.
La troisième saison de Color Matters – Masters of Color se poursuit avec un nouvel épisode consacré à John Quartel, responsable de l'Imaging Science chez Company 3. Après avoir découvert le travail des coloristes et leurs choix artistiques dans les épisodes 1 et 2, cette nouvelle vidéo s'intéresse à la science qui se cache derrière les images des plus grandes productions hollywoodiennes.
De Top Gun: Maverick à F1
John Quartel explique notamment comment la science de l'image repose sur trois dimensions essentielles : la couleur, l'espace et le temps. Autant de paramètres qu'il faut maîtriser pour préserver les intentions du réalisateur, depuis le tournage jusqu'à la diffusion du film.
Il revient sur les défis techniques rencontrés sur Top Gun: Maverick, où les équipes ont dû intégrer plusieurs caméras dans les cockpits des avions de chasse. Chaque caméra possédant ses propres caractéristiques colorimétriques, il a fallu harmoniser les images pour obtenir un rendu cohérent.
Même problématique sur F1, avec des volumes considérables de séquences filmées par les caméras embarquées. John Quartel évoque é…

articles.title: DHS bans DeepSeek products across US federal civilian agencies
articles.summary:
The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is ordering federal civilian agencies to stop using DeepSeek products and remove them from government systems.
The order also covers products from the Chinese AI company's affiliates and third-party products and services built using DeepSeek technology.
DeepSeek (Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co., Ltd) develops large language models and offers a chatbot, API services, and models suitable for coding and reasoning tasks.
Its AI tools became extremely popular early on, but were but were soon followed by reports of security risks [1, 2, 3, 4] and concerns about the potential for Chinese authorities to access users’ conversations.
The DHS is now taking regulatory action to limit the use of DeepSeek and derivatives on critical systems in the United States, and has issued a notice of order for agencies to:
- Immediately exclude covered products from procurement, including approved-product lists and purchasing marketplaces.
- Immediately remove covered products from agency IT systems, or seek an exception.
- Submit any exception requests within 60 days of the order’s issuance, explaining the justification and proposed risk mitigations. CISA will review requests and issue written approvals or denials.
The order applies to federal civilian agencies within DHS’s authority and is not a general ban on private or consumer use.
DHS explained that the order stems from concerns about the Chinese government accessing DeepSeek infrastru…

articles.title: Mods can almost double DLSS 5 performance through Foveation, reducing resolution at the edges of frames — technique makes DLSS 5 possible on high-resolution ultrawide monitors
articles.summary:
Mods can almost double DLSS 5 performance through Foveation, reducing resolution at the edges of frames — technique makes DLSS 5 possible on high-resolution ultrawide monitors
This might actually make DLSS 5 more accessible.
Popular graphics post-processing injector software ReShade, commonly used to mod DLSS 5 into unsupported games, now has a foveated imaging add-on, including another standalone project that doesn't need precursor software, allowing DLSS 5 to affect only what's in view, reducing GPU load and increasing FPS.
Foveated imaging is nothing new; it's a technique that's been used in VR to increase performance. It works by only rendering what's in view, often increasing the resolution in the center and reducing it at the edges. Our eyes work in a similar way, with the clearest image in a small area in the center of your vision, blurring on the edges. With foveated rendering, you barely notice the lower-resolution edges as the peripheral vision is less concerned with fine details.
Instead of varying the resolution of the image, however, it varies the level of detail in DLSS 5 Neural Rendering. DLSS NR loads a whole AI model into your GPU and renders images in real time, making it a resource-intensive task; but the task is minimized greatly when most of the detail is only asked for in the middle of the image. articles.title: Elon Musk quer doar ações da SpaceX para crianças nos EUA • Tecnoblog
articles.summary:
Elon Musk quer doar ações da SpaceX para crianças nos EUA
CEO da empresa estaria disposto a ceder US$ 10,5 bilhões em programa de contas para crianças e adolescentes.
Elon Musk afirmou que pretende doar ações da SpaceX para crianças dos Estados Unidos. Embora não tenha detalhado como a iniciativa funcionaria, a contribuição pode chegar a US$ 10,5 bilhões (R$ 52,5 bilhões). Em uma publicação no X, o bilionário disse que a proposta seria viabilizada pelo programa Trump Accounts, criado para incentivar a independência financeira de crianças nascidas no país durante o segundo mandato do atual presidente.
Além de Musk, a iniciativa já conta com doações da própria presidente da SpaceX, Gwynne Shotwell, e da gigante de semicondutores Micron, que já investiram US$ 6,2 bilhões (R$ 31 bilhões) e US$ 250 milhões (R$ 1,2 bilhão), respectivamente. A medida surge em meio às eleições de meio de mandato dos Estados Unidos.
No post feito no X/Twitter, o também CEO da Tesla não deu detalhes de quanto será doado ou qual faixa etária vai receber o projeto. A estimativa dos US$ 10,5 bilhões se dá a partir do valor de cada ação da SpaceX hoje (cerca de US$ 147, ou R$ 740 em conversão direta) e as 72 milhões de crianças nos Estados Unidos. Segundo o bilionário, a doação seria feita a partir do ano que vem, e seria “a primeira de muitas”.

articles.title: Google has joined Amazon in attacking Nvidia's stronghold with AI app developers | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
On Tuesday, Google announced that TorchTPU, its long-awaited version of PyTorch, is now available as an open-source project. With this, Google joins Amazon in trying to break Nvidia’s stranglehold on the AI industry, where most AI apps are written by default to run on Nvidia’s chips, or GPUs.
PyTorch is the popular open-source toolkit that AI app developers and startups use to build, train, and run AI models. It is, by some accounts, used by 85% of the AI apps. PyTorch was originally developed by Meta (then Facebook) in 2016, long before the world had an inkling that LLMs would change the world. At the time, Nvidia’s GPUs were already the standard hardware for AI research, so many of PyTorch’s features were built to work specifically with them. In 2022, Meta turned PyTorch over to the Linux Foundation, a nonprofit that manages many important open source projects.
Google’s version, TorchTPU, lets AI apps run on Google’s AI chips, called Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). It also makes it easy to move existing PyTorch apps to TPUs and, therefore, to Google Cloud. Developers can do this with a simple configuration change and no re-writing of their apps.
Amazon made a similar announcement Monday, when it released its own version of PyTorch, called TorchNeuron. TorchNeuron allows AI apps to be ported to Amazon’s homegrown AI chip, Trainium, and to AWS with no rewriting. Amazon also said it going even further in its effort to loosen Nvidia’s hold on PyTorch. articles.title: Air Canada now charges you $30 fee for phone bookings
articles.summary:
Air Canada has started charging customers a $30 fee for booking flights over the phone.
As spotted by CP24, the change went into effect on Oct. 15, per Air Canada’s website. On the page, the airline notes that this $30 (plus applicable taxes) charge will apply to each passenger on new bookings made by phone. It adds that the booking fee will continue to apply for Aeroplan flight reward bookings.
Fliers will still be able to call Air Canada for support with existing reservations, travel disruptions and other inquiries without paying any fees.
In an FAQ on its site, Air Canada says the reason it has introduced this fee is to push its self-serve digital tools.
“Air Canada’s website and mobile app make it easy to book and manage your travel,” writes the airline. “Using these digital tools for everyday travel needs helps reduce wait times and allows our Contact Centre agents to focus their expertise on situations that require personalized support. ”
It should be noted that other Canadian airlines WestJet and Flair already charge for phone bookings, although their prices are $25 each.
While most people likely book their flights online anyway, it’s always annoying to see more fees added onto services, especially when, in this case, it’s literally for the purposes of giving money to Air Canada. If nothing else, charging people for speaking to an agent isn’t as bad as Cineplex, which for the past couple of years has charged a $1.50 booking fee for online purchases where it saves money…

articles.title: Europe's four largest carriers want to build a Starlink rival, but they don't have satellites
articles.summary:
In brief: In another sign of Europe's continuing push away from reliance on US tech, four of the continent's biggest mobile operators are considering joining forces to create a Starlink competitor. The proposed service would connect phones directly to satellites, helping fill coverage gaps while giving European carriers an alternative to Elon Musk's network.
Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefónica, and Vodafone have signed a letter of intent to explore a joint bid for Mobile Satellite Services spectrum in Europe. The agreement, announced on Monday, is an early step toward offering direct-to-device connectivity through their existing mobile networks.
The aim is to reach areas where conventional mobile infrastructure falls short. Starlink already offers similar coverage through partnerships with carriers including T-Mobile in the US and O2 in the UK.
There is, however, a fairly significant piece of the plan missing: the satellites. The four operators don't intend to invest directly in a constellation themselves. Instead, they would build ground infrastructure and establish coordination and monitoring operations in Europe, with a satellite partner providing the orbiting hardware. That partner has yet to be selected.
The companies say other mobile operators would also be able to access the service on equal terms. They want the project to improve coverage in underserved areas, protect critical communications, and make public networks more resilient. Existing satellite partnerships wo…

articles.title: El Niño : la Nasa détecte les signes d'un épisode « potentiellement historique » dans l'océan Pacifique
articles.summary:
« Un phénomène plus rare qu’une éclipse solaire et plus puissant que n’importe quel système orageux » : c’est en ces termes que la Nasa décrit l’évolution actuelle d’El Niño. Le 15 octobre 2026, l’agence spatiale a attiré l’attention sur ses observations par satellite du phénomène, qui s’annonce comme l’un des plus intenses depuis des décennies.
La Nasa confirme ainsi ce qu’annoncent les agences météorologiques depuis le printemps. Depuis juin 2026, le phénomène climatique El Niño a officiellement commencé. Selon l’Organisation météorologique mondiale (OMM), El Niño devrait se maintenir jusqu’en février 2027. Désormais, c’est la Nasa qui indique que ses satellites détectent des signes d’un épisode d’El Niño potentiellement « historique » cet automne.
El Niño revient environ tous les 2 à 7 ans, rappelle la Nasa, mais l’épisode de 2026 sort du lot par son intensité. En octobre, l’Agence américaine d’observation océanique et atmosphérique (NOAA) estimait à 83 % la probabilité qu’il s’agisse du plus fort El Niño depuis 1950.
El Niño : de quoi parle-t-on exactement ?
El Niño est une composante d’un phénomène climatique naturel, El Niño-oscillation australe (ENSO). L’ENSO correspond à des variations des températures de surface de l’océan, dans le centre et l’est du Pacifique. El Niño en est la phase chaude, La Niña la phase froide, et le troisième état est appelé « ENSO neutre ».

articles.title: Des hackers détournent des serveurs Plex non mis à jour pour miner des cryptos, le vôtre est-il en danger ?
articles.summary:
Plus de deux mois après la publication des correctifs, des pirates exploitent plusieurs failles de Plex Media Server. Les machines compromises servent à miner des cryptomonnaies, mais aussi à relayer du trafic Internet à l'insu de leurs propriétaires.
Début septembre, Plex appelait une nouvelle fois ses utilisateurs et utilisatrices à installer une mise à jour de sécurité sur leurs serveurs multimédias. Si l'éditeur se montrait discret sur la nature des vulnérabilités corrigées, il ne faisait alors état d'aucune exploitation active. C'est désormais chose faite depuis la publication, le 16 octobre dernier, d'un code permettant d'exploiter quatre de ces failles pour exécuter du code à distance sur un serveur, sans authentification. Dès le lendemain, un chercheur observait des tentatives d'intrusion sur un serveur leurre, tandis que des propriétaires d'installations non patchées signalaient à leur tour des activités suspectes.
Plex2Shell, quatre vulnérabilités exploitées en chaîne
Baptisée Plex2Shell, cette méthode d'attaque repose sur l'enchaînement de quatre vulnérabilités, référencées CVE-2026-96652, CVE-2026-96654, CVE-2026-96655 et CVE-2026-96656. Leur exploitation combinée permet de contourner les contrôles d'accès de Plex, de récupérer le jeton d'administration du serveur, puis d'y déposer un fichier malveillant que le logiciel exécutera avec les privilèges du processus Media Server.

Ether es un token que se utiliza específicamente en la blockchain ethereum para pagar transacciones. articles.title: Revolut victime d'une panne majeure : les paiements touchés, la banque réagit
articles.summary:
« Nous pouvons confirmer que tout l’argent et les données de nos clients sont en sécurité » : Revolut a posté un message sur le réseau social X, alors qu’un nombre conséquent de ses clients européens n’arrive plus à utiliser ses services. Que ce soit les paiements par carte ou l’accès à l’application, Revolut semble être à l’arrêt. L’origine de la panne se situerait au niveau de l’un de ses prestataires.
Revolut victime d’une panne majeure
Depuis environ 8 heures du matin, la néobanque Revolut est victime d’une panne majeure. Un nombre conséquent de ses clients ne parviennent pas à payer par carte et à accéder à l’application. Le problème toucherait plusieurs pays européens, dont la France. Sur sa page de suivi de l’état du système, Revolut signale une panne touchant l’ensemble de ses 31 services surveillés.

Welp, time to bring out that xkcd comic out again.
Modern computing systems and devices typically require pieces of crucial open-source software, typically maintained by unpaid or low-paid volunteers. Recently, a report collated a list of critical open-source projects, noting which of them are chronically underfunded and/or understaffed. The information is sobering: 11 out of 23 of the listed projects currently only have one or two maintainers, and funding is generally scarce and sometimes nonexistent.
The Data Drop's report on open-source maintainers identifies that having only one or two sets of eyes on critical pieces of software means that sooner or later something breaks — and it tends to do so in spectacular fashion, given its ubiquity. So, what happens when these projects, which are widely used across software, go underfunded or understaffed?
Lessons from the past
In 2014, the same year as Heartbleed, Shellshock made waves: a vulnerability in the Bash shell that's present in Linux, macOS, and Unix-type systems. The problem was traced back to a line of code present since 1989, displaying how even software that's thought to have all the bugs hammered out of it can still fall prey to attacks. articles.title: Quantum error correction goes well beyond breakeven
articles.summary:
Running complicated algorithms on quantum computing hardware is going to require the use of logical qubits, where collections of hardware qubits are linked together in ways that allow errors to be detected and corrected. In general, the more hardware qubits you dedicate to each logical qubit, the better the chances are of identifying errors. But, given that the hardware qubits are prone to errors, adding more of them also increases the probability that errors will occur. If the hardware error rate is too high, then growing the logical qubit will only make matters worse.
Fortunately, several companies have demonstrated hardware where the error rate is not too high. Several demonstrations show logical qubits are beyond the breakeven point, where adding more qubits improves performance. The problem is that the improvement isn’t very dramatic. To lower error rates to levels we’ll need to run complex algorithms, we’d have to add a completely impractical number of qubits to each logical qubit.
On Monday, Quantinuum announced that its current generation of hardware is capable of scaling well beyond the breakeven point. Each step up in the size of logical qubits improved some measures of their performance by a factor of over 10.
Error correction codes and scaling

articles.title: AI-assisted vibe coding brings Thunderbolt 4 support to Windows 98 SE

The takeaway: Vibe coding is viewed negatively by many, but when dedicating resources to a specific project isn't feasible, few alternatives exist. Microsoft, for example, doesn't have the time or resources to create modern drivers for operating systems they've long moved on from… but AI has no problem crafting code for legacy versions of Windows.
A developer by the name of Yeo Kheng Meng recently commissioned AI to create a driver that enables generic USB 3.x, USB4, and Thunderbolt 3/4 host controllers to work on ancient operating systems including Window 98 SE, ME, 2000, XP, Vista, and 7.
Dated versions of Windows barely make a blip on the OS market share radar, so why should anyone even care about something like this? Well, despite the low percentage of overall users, there are still lots of retro computing enthusiasts out there actively using older computers running legacy hardware and software. Being able to take advantage of modern connectivity is just icing on the cake for them.
Even if you aren't interested in this particular driver, there's a lot to take away from a story like this. Vibe coding gets trashed in the mainstream as a lazy way to approach a coding problem but as mentioned, not everyone has the time or resources to devote human programmers to every project. Tasks are often tackled based on priority, and making a driver for retro computing fans likely isn't going to rank high on that list.

GM is closing a battery assembly plant south of Detroit, a spokesperson confirmed to TechCrunch.
The Brownstown Battery Assembly Plant assembled battery packs for Cadillac’s flagship EV, the Celestiq, and both electric drive units (the motors that power the car) and battery packs for the Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray, a plug-in hybrid version of its famous sports car. Automotive News first reported the closure.
The closure is not related to GM’s electric vehicle strategy, the spokesperson said. Instead, GM leased the site, and the lease was nearing its end.
The employees and work at Brownstown will be moved to other GM facilities, though the company would not confirm which ones.
Like many automakers, GM’s electrification strategy was thrown a curveball after the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, the sweeping federal law signed last year, repealed incentives to produce and sell EVs.
Since then, the company has pared back its public comments on EVs, though it hasn’t given up on full electrification.
GM continues to produce a range of EVs, including the Chevrolet Silverado EV and the limited-time-only Chevrolet Bolt. It also continues researching new battery chemistries, including lithium-manganese-rich and sodium-ion, and it’s rolling out a new $900 million facility to speed commercialization.

The operation was revealed just days after separate Ukrainian drones designed for casualty evacuation were deployed for frontline testing—taking a step beyond the US military’s decades of experimentation with similar concepts.
The drone evacuation of the injured soldier took place at an undisclosed time and place on the frontline where the presence of Russian drones and landmines made it impractical to send in a wheeled ground robot, according to The Kyiv Independent. On October 19, Ukraine’s Army shared a video of the drone evacuation, showing the wounded soldier securing himself in a harness suspended beneath a heavy hexacopter drone with six rotors before being flown to safety.
“This is a historic event, the next stage of evacuating the wounded, which we will all come to,” said Napalm, a programmer of the 92nd separate assault brigade’s unmanned ground systems company, who went by his callsign per Ukrainian military practice, in a statement. “Now the serious systematic work begins, so that such missions are carried out constantly.”
Flying out the wounded
To perform the improvised aerial evacuation, the 92nd brigade prepared and tested a heavy hexacopter drone—the Heavy Shot AYUDAG 6 model—provided for free by the Ukrainian manufacturer Gurzuf Defence. Special carabiners were first delivered to the wounded soldier so he could att…

articles.title: ChatGPT's Chrome extension can now control tabs, download files, and fill out forms
articles.summary:
In a nutshell: OpenAI has released a major update to its ChatGPT browser extension, bringing deeper integration with Google Chrome. The extension can now access content from open webpages, analyze information, and complete tasks directly in the browser. The update also introduces new voice features and support for several additional languages.
ChatGPT's Chrome extension gained the ability to access content from open tabs last July. The latest update introduces two distinct AI modes, Chat and Work, allowing ChatGPT to interact with browser tabs and perform a wide range of tasks, including filling out online forms using information from documents stored on the device.
In Chat mode, the AI can read content from open tabs to analyze information and answer questions based on the active page context. For example, users can compare prices, delivery times, return policies, and other factors for products listed across different shopping sites.
In Work mode, ChatGPT can control the browser to send messages, download files, and group open tabs by topic. It can also fill out forms using information gathered online or extracted from files stored on the computer. Once a form is completed, users can review it manually before submitting it.

articles.title: Une mission révolutionnaire : mais que va faire le rover français IDEFIX sur la lune de Mars, au juste ?
articles.summary:
Le Japon vient de lancer MMX, une mission inédite pour ramener sur Terre des morceaux de Phobos, l’une des deux lunes de Mars. À son bord, le petit rover franco-allemand, IDEFIX, jouera un rôle crucial.
Mars n’est pas seule : notre voisine est accompagnée de deux petites lunes, Phobos et Deimos. Découvertes en 1877 par l’astronome américain Asaph Hall, elles ressemblent à deux gros cailloux difformes, souvent comparés à des pommes de terre.
Phobos, la plus grande, mesure environ 22 kilomètres de large. Et elle se rapproche inexorablement de Mars et finira, dans 50 millions d’années, par s’écraser sur la planète ou se disloquer en anneau. Deimos, elle, atteint 15 kilomètres seulement. Leur origine reste, à ce jour, un mystère : sont-elles les débris d’un impact géant sur Mars, ou des astéroïdes capturés par sa gravité ?
IDEFIX, un éclaireur sur Phobos
C’est justement la question à laquelle va tenter de répondre la mission MMX de la JAXA, l’agence spatiale japonaise. Elle a décollé ce 19 octobre à bord d’une fusée H3, depuis le centre spatial de Tanegashima, dans le sud-ouest de l’archipel.
La sonde va voyager environ dix mois dans l’espace pour rejoindre la planète rouge, où elle doit arriver en août 2027. Elle se placera ensuite autour de Phobos et y restera près de trois ans. C’est à ce moment-là qu’IDEFIX entrera en scène. Ce petit rover a été conçu par l’agence spatiale allemande (DLR) et le CNES. De la taille d’une caisse de boissons, il pèse 25 kilos sur Terre. articles.title: Netflix : nouveau séisme sur la plateforme avec un changement majeur en interne
articles.summary:
Netflix n’a même pas attendu de présenter ses résultats trimestriels aux analystes de Wall Street, prévus ce mardi 20 octobre. Face à une action en baisse de plus de 20 % depuis janvier et à un temps de visionnage qui n’a progressé que de 2 % au premier semestre, le co-CEO de Netflix, Ted Sarandos, a sorti le couperet. Vingt-quatre heures après l’éviction brutale de sa directrice des contenus Bela Bajaria, c’est Dan Lin (qui s’occupait du cinéma) que Ted Sarandos a appelé vendredi pour lui annoncer son renvoi, officialisé ce lundi 19 octobre.
La fin de l’ère de l’austérité pour Netflix : Dan Lin et le piège du « zéro chèque en blanc »
L’aventure aura duré deux ans et demi, soit la moitié de son contrat de cinq ans, pour celui qui avait été nommé en février 2024 pour succéder à Scott Stuber. À son arrivée, Lin incarnait la rupture : fini la distribution de billets verts à l’aveugle, fini le gavage des stars hollywoodiennes et la promesse intenable d’un film inédit par semaine.
En juin, dans le New York Times, Dan Lin affirmait que Netflix avait « accepté » de ne plus travailler avec les cinéastes qui tiennent à une sortie en salles. Mais à Hollywood, la rigueur budgétaire se paie cash dès que les chiffres de visionnage ne suivent plus. Malgré la réorganisation des équipes par genre et quelques sorties en salles à titre d’essai, Lin n’a pas trouvé l’équilibre entre films taillés pour le streaming et sorties au cinéma, principal motif de son renvoi selon les sources du média amé…

articles.title: Homebase launches AI assistant to take on scheduling and payroll for small business owners - SiliconANGLE

Homebase launches AI assistant to take on scheduling and payroll for small business owners
Small business team management company Homebase today introduced Homebase Assistant, an artificial intelligence tool for owners who run hourly teams without a back office.
Homebase bills it as the only AI built specifically for that market. Assistant targets the desk work that comes with running a small business.
In Homebase’s telling, most owners are on the floor all day, so payroll and scheduling wait until they can get to a computer at night. The company said a job such as building a schedule or writing a job post can drop from hours to minutes, with the owner still signing off on the result.
Founder and Chief Executive John Waldmann said every owner he talks to has “the same 6 a.m. moment,” when an employee calls out sick and the day becomes a hunt for a replacement. In his view, most AI tools would stop at telling the owner that a shift is uncovered. He called the Homebase approach “AI that acts.”
In the sick-call scenario Waldmann described, the assistant works out which employees could cover. None of them is contacted before the owner gives the go-ahead, at which point the software takes over the outreach until somebody accepts the shift.
On the payroll side, timecards get a check before each pay run. Homebase said the assistant catches missing punches and similar errors early enough that an owner can sort them out in one go. Overtime trends get the same early warning, as do gaps…

articles.title: Sicherheitslücke in Routern entdeckt: Wie ein 16 Jahre alter Fehler erneut zum Problem wird

Router vernetzen zahlreiche Haushalte mit dem Internet. Sie können aber schnell zum Einfallstor für Cyberkriminelle werden, wenn du nicht die richtigen Einstellungen am Router vornimmst. Gleiches gilt, wenn es eine Lücke im System der Router gibt, die lange Zeit unerkannt bleibt. So soll es laut einem Sicherheitsforscher schon seit 2010 der Fall sein. Laut ihm sind von der Lücke potenziell Millionen Geräte betroffen.
Neue Router-Sicherheitslücke: Welche Gefahr droht
Die Warnung stammt vom belgischen Sicherheitsforscher Quentin Kaiser, der die Sicherheitslücke „WPSplinter“ getauft hat. Im Grunde handelt es sich dabei um zwei Fehler, die in der Software von Broadcom zu finden sind. Broadcoms Wi-Fi-Implementierung wird laut Kaiser von dutzenden Routerherstellern genutzt. Dadurch finden sich die Fehler in hunderten Produkten und potenziell in „Millionen von Broadcom-basierten Access-Points weltweit“.
Die Fehler sorgen dafür, dass sich Unbefugte über WPS (Wi-Fi Protected Setup) Zugriff auf die Router verschaffen können. Über das Feature können Endgeräte und Router ohne Passworteingabe miteinander verknüpft werden, indem eine WPS-Taste auf dem Router gedrückt wird, während das Endgerät ebenfalls einen WPS-Prozess startet. Laut Kaiser kann eine manipulierte WPS-Nachricht eingeschleust werden, um den Speicher der Router zu verändern.

Justement, Spotify a décidé de sévir concernant son abonnement Premium Famille, qui permet de partager un compte Premium avec les membres de sa famille qui « vivent sous le même toit ». La plateforme de streaming musical semble estimer que trop de personnes partagent un compte Famille Premium, sans vivre sous le même toit. Elle a donc décidé de mettre en place un nouveau système de vérification.
Un QR code dynamique à scanner
Spotify a décidé de s’attaquer aux personnes qui partagent un abonnement Premium Famille, sans vivre sous le même toit. Comme le rapporte Android Authority, des utilisateurs de Reddit signalent une demande de vérification de la part de la plateforme de streaming musical. Pour être plus précis, ceux qui bénéficient d’un abonnement Premium Famille doivent scanner un QR code avec le propriétaire du compte Premium.
Point important : il s’agit d’un QR code dynamique, autrement dit, il est renouvelé toutes les quelques secondes, ce qui complique sensiblement la réalisation d’une capture d’écran pour ensuite le scanner. De ce fait, ce système de vérification par scan de QR code dynamique permet de vérifier que les deux personnes se situent à proximité l’une de l’autre, et donc vivent bel et bien sous le même toit.

articles.title: Google DeepMind presume de haber batido a Minecraft con agentes controlados por Gemini 4 Argon en apenas 27 horas
articles.summary:
'Minecraft' no es sólo uno de los juegos más exitosos de la historia y una base genial tanto para divertirse como para aprender. El título de Mojang lleva años usándose para medir de qué son capaces los modelos de inteligencia artificial y Google Deepmind acaba de anotarse un tanto: su Gemini 4 Argon ha completado 'Minecraft' de principio a fin in intervención humana.
Y parece que esta IA lo ha hecho sin trampas.
En corto. Cuatro agentes basados en Gemini 4 Argon derrotaron al Ender Dragon en 27 horas y 14 minutos. Se trata del jefe final del juego y los resultados se publicaron en un paper en arXiv en el que los autores son algunos de los responsables de Google Deepmind.
Se trata de uno de los últimos modelos de la compañía, uno que lleva semanas en un circuito cerrado para que expertos en ciberseguridad lo pusieran a prueba, pero que se liberó a suscriptores de pago el pasado 13 de octubre. Ahora bien, tiene cierto truco.
A ciegas. La prueba se realizó en un mundo generado al azar, en dificultad fácil y con los comandos de trampa desactivados. A los agentes sólo se les dio el objetivo de matar a la dragona, sin otras instrucciones, herramientas específicas para Minecraft o estrategias para acelerar el progreso. Cada uno de los agentes controlaban a un jugador mediante Mineflayer, una bibloteca de código abierto para crear bots del juego y, para actuar, vibecodeaban un programa corto en Java que era el que emitía las órdenes.

articles.title: Cementerios tecnológicos o museos vivos: así sobreviven los dispositivos del pasado en las calles de Bogotá
articles.summary:
En nuestro presente digital, la palabra actualización se convirtió en un término indispensable. Los grandes avances tecnológicos requieren constantes mejoras en los sistemas operativos, por lo que resultan impulsando un ciclo de consumo constante que cada vez más se parece a una obsolescencia programada.
Pero hace un par de décadas, la industria operaba bajo otra lógica, a mayor resistencia, mejor producto. Fabricaban dispositivos pensados para perdurar en los años, e incluso algunos lo hicieron con el mítico Nokia 1100, que evoca, entre nostalgia y risas, la imagen de un teléfono que podría soportar cualquier golpe.
Afirmar que todo pasado fue mejor implica ignorar un presente dinámico, marcado por un desarrollo acelerado que ha dado lugar a dispositivos tan innovadores que hoy se consideran indispensables en la vida cotidiana.
Más allá del avance en electrodomésticos y del debate sobre el paso del tiempo y la funcionalidad, existen dispositivos que permanecen en la memoria colectiva, pero que, debido a la evolución tecnológica, dejaron de ser de uso común. Esto invita a preguntarse dónde concluyó su vida útil y qué ocurrió con ellos tras su retirada del día a día.
En el norte de Bogotá, en un mercado popular, o como algunos prefieren llamarlo, “mercado de las pulgas”, un hombre de 84 años de edad atiende un puesto que bien podría ser un cementerio de dispositivos tecnológicos. Development platform Zeabur has disclosed details of a cybersecurity incident in which an attacker used leaked internal credentials stored in plaintext to compromise its infrastructure and steal over 3.2 million environment variable records and information for 321,810 accounts.
The attackers used stolen administrator credentials and cloud access keys to compromise Zeabur’s shared hosting infrastructure and dedicated servers, eventually gaining access to its production database.
“On October 14–15, 2026, an attacker used leaked Zeabur internal credentials to break into the shared cluster, some Dedicated Servers, and Zeabur internal systems, and eventually read the platform database,” Zeabur’s announcement reads.
Zeabur is a developer hosting and deployment platform that lets developers connect a GitHub repository and have the platform handle deployment, databases, HTTPS, and infrastructure management.
In late August 2026, the company suffered another security breach when hackers exploited a flaw in a customer’s NextChat application and then moved through poorly isolated internal systems.
This led to the theft of AWS credentials and access to the production database, exposing account information, API keys, and other secrets stored there.
In the latest incident, Zeabur says the compromise was broader, affecting shared clusters across nine regions, 321,810 accounts, and roughly 3.2 million environment-variable records.

articles.title: Does anyone actually want to win the medium-lift race in the United States?
articles.summary:
It has been 13 years since the debut of a new medium-lift rocket in the United States, the Antares vehicle developed by Orbital Sciences Corporation.
The initial 100-series variant of the Antares rocket was kind of a hot mess. The rocket used old Soviet engines built during the era when Apollo astronauts were landing on the Moon. Decades later, in the 1990s, Aerojet acquired the engines and refurbished them for a rocket that would launch in the 2010s. Predictably, on the fifth launch of an Antares rocket in 2014, it exploded.
The Antares vehicle is the last of a dying breed of medium-lift rockets—defined as having a lift capacity of 2 to 20 metric tons—in the United States. Nearly a decade and a half later there is a new generation of medium-lift vehicles coming online, and they are starkly different from Antares, which had not just Russian engines but a core stage manufactured in Ukraine.
Four forthcoming rockets all have engines built by the rocket’s manufacturer in the United States. Each of these companies has taken various lessons from SpaceX’s successful Falcon 9 rocket, arguably the most important of which is to build as much of one’s rocket, and particularly the engines, in-house as possible to control timelines and costs.
Now, with SpaceX pulling the Falcon 9 rocket from the commercial market as soon as 2028, the “race” to bring new medium-lift capacity into service is for more than bragging rights. There are fortunes to be made, and commercial space startups to be s…

articles.title: GTA 6 is on track to smash records as pre-orders exceed 6 million copies

Forward-looking: Grand Theft Auto VI is expected to be the biggest video game launch of 2026 and, quite possibly, the most successful entertainment launch in history. With one month to go before its November 19 release on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles, market intelligence firm Sensor Tower has shared its estimates for the game's pre-orders.
As of October 20, Rockstar has pre-sold an estimated 6.45 million copies of the game – earning roughly $630 million in the process. articles.title: Après les violents pillages, pourquoi l’état d’urgence ne permettrait pas de bloquer les réseaux sociaux
articles.summary:
Après les pillages du 17 octobre, certains, comme Bruno Retailleau, réclame l’état d’urgence et le gouvernement le garde en réserve. Ce régime d’exception issu d’une loi de 1955 permettrait surtout des mesures individuelles, mais pas de couper librement les réseaux sociaux.
Depuis les pillages qui ont suivi les manifestations du 17 octobre, l'état d'urgence s'est invité dans de nombreuses conversations, des plateaux télé aux fils d'actualité, aussi bien c'est ceux qui réclament son instauration que ceux qui le vilipendent. Le gouvernement de Sébastien Lecornu a préféré miser lundi soir des couvre-feux localisés à Paris, Lyon ou Lille, tout en gardant le régime d'exception sous le coude « si c'est nécessaire ». Entre la loi de 1955, la jurisprudence du Conseil d’État sur TikTok et le règlement européen DSA sur le services numériques, les marges de manœuvre de l’exécutif sont pourtant plus étroites qu’il n’y paraît.
L'état d’urgence, un pouvoir d’exception, pas un chèque en blanc
Cette fameuse loi de 1955, justement, mérite qu'on s'y arrête. Votée le 3 avril 1955, en pleine guerre d'Algérie, elle a donné naissance à un régime d'exception que la Constitution ne mentionne même pas, et qui ne peut être déclenché qu'en cas de péril imminent lié à des atteintes graves à l'ordre public. Le président le décrète en conseil des ministres, pour douze jours maximum. Au-delà, seul le Parlement peut le prolonger par une loi, qui devient caduque quinze jours après une démission du gouverneme…

articles.title: Marie Curie y Einstein se escribieron cartas durante más de 20 años. 100 años después podemos leer lo que se decían
articles.summary:
El 7 de julio de 1922, Marie Curie le escribió a Albert Einstein para echarle la bronca. Con buenas formas, sí; pero bronca al fin y al cabo: Curie le llegaba a decir que le había causado una 'gran decepción'.
Durante 21 años, dos de los científicos más importantes de la historia se escribieron cartas en las que apenas se hablaba de física. Lo que hicieron fue cubrirse las espaldas. Y ahora, un siglo después, podemos leer la historia completa.
¿"Una gran decepción"? Tres días antes de aquella carta del 7 de julio, Einstein le había contado a Curie que iba a dimitir de la comisión de cooperación intelectual de la Sociedad de Naciones. Le confesó las razones, pero le pidió que no se las contara a nadie.
El 24 de junio habían asesinado en Berlín al ministro de Exteriores de la República de Weimar, Walther Rathenau, un viejo amigo de Einstein. Aquello había acabado por desmoralizarle. Y, precisamente por eso, Curie le cantaba las cuarenta. Claro que había corrientes de opinión extremadamente dañinas, pero a su juicio había que combatirlas y, de hecho, estaba convencida de que el mismo Rathenau estaría de acuerdo con ella. ¿No había alguna posibilidad de que cambiara de idea?
Un libro para la historia de la ciencia. No ha sido fácil recopilar la correspondencia entre ambos. Durante años, se han rastreado archivos en Jerusalén, París, Zúrich, Princeton, Düsseldorf o Varsovia y apenas se han encontrado 32 cartas. articles.title: Chris Lattner: AI Code Generation Doesn't Solve Software Engineering - EE Times
articles.summary:
For AI chip companies, the promise of AI-based coding agents is compelling: generate the low-level kernels needed to get a model running on new hardware, optimize them for performance, and do it without the software engineering resources traditionally required.
But according to Chris Lattner, CEO of AI software startup Modular (recently acquired by Qualcomm, where he now serves as executive VP of software engineering), chip companies should be wary of the limits of AI code generation. Making a kernel run fast is a very different problem from building software infrastructure we can depend on, he told EE Times in an exclusive interview.
“Agents are good, but they’re like anything else; it’s a tool, and you have to use it the right way,” Lattner said. “What I’ve seen with agents is they make tons of throwaway code. So, if you’re building a product, you don’t want to agent-generate everything.”
Agentic code generation makes sense for projects that are well-defined and limited in scope (e.g., “make this kernel go fast”), which can be quantified, measured, and validated, Lattner said, but bigger projects require product design and software engineering and can’t be delegated to agents.
“If you’re a startup and you only care about getting one model working, or getting it to go fast, [then go ahead,] use AI tools to prove it’s possible,” he said. “But that’s not going to be great for when you want to sell your chip to someone else, and they want to run a model you don’t have access to…

Many enterprise services currently host MCP servers to provide access to business systems, and these servers expose tools that let agents interact with basic and complex controls.
Anthropic PBC introduced MCP in 2024 as an open-source standard, often described as a USB-C port for AI. It acts like a single, universal access point for AI models and agents to plug into databases, local files, search engines, business data and application programming interfaces to access resources.

The sort of work that used to fall to integration specialists can now be completed by AI agents such as Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot and Cursor autonomously.

articles.title: La psicología sabe por qué algunas personas aman los días de lluvia mientras el resto del mundo se queja
articles.summary:
Hay gente que adora esos días en los que la lluvia cae en la calle y el mejor plan que tienen en mente es quedarse en casa mientras escuchan el agua caer. Para muchos, esto puede asociarse a una personalidad melancólica, pero la psicología nos sugiere que disfrutar de la lluvia tiene mucho que ver con la forma en la que nuestro cerebro procesa los estímulos de baja intensidad y busca el alivio del estrés.
Odiar el verano. Antes de entrar en el porqué ocurre esto a los amantes de la lluvia, hay que desmentir el hecho de que a todo el mundo le afecte el clima de la misma manera. Aquí tenemos de referencia un estudio de 2008 que analizó a más de 1.200 personas y concluyó que el efecto medio del tiempo sobre el estado de ánimo es pequeño, pero con una gran variación individual. Aunque curiosamente, se desmitifica la idea de la "relajación profunda" bajo la lluvia, puesto que la falta de luz solar se asociaba directamente con un mayor cansancio.
Fue tres años más tarde cuando un nuevo estudio nos reveló mucho más al analizar a casi 500 adolescentes y a sus madres junto a sus perfiles climáticos. Uno de ellos fue bautizado como 'Summer Haters', el cual estaba representado por el 27% de los adolescentes y el 12% de las madres, que se sentían más felices y satisfechos con más lluvia, menos sol y temperaturas más bajas.

articles.title: The Internet goes on high alert after discovery of 8 compromised TLS certs
articles.summary:
Security personnel around the world are on high alert Tuesday following the discovery of eight TLS certificates with private keys so weak they could allow anyone to mint trusted browser and app credentials for any site on the Internet.
As of late morning Tuesday, browser makers and some major apps and programming languages had blocked all eight of the intermediate certificates. There are no reports of certificate transparency logs, which track the issuance of all browser-trusted certificates, showing the compromised keys being used maliciously. The threat remains far from over, however, because it will be hard and time-consuming to update other key parts of the Internet, such as Linux distributions and embedded and Internet of Things devices.
One word: bonkers
The eight intermediate certificates belong to India-based certificate authority eMudhra Limited. An informal advisory published to emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com over on Tuesday posted the message “We have a problem here – Wayne.” The words were digitally signed using the private key of one of the eMudhra certificates. With proof that the reporting party had control of the key, defenders scrambled because the same key could be used to sign unauthorized certificates that would be trusted by millions of servers worldwide.

CON, PRN und NUL: Warum du Dateien in Windows 11 nicht so benennen darfst
Obwohl Windows 11 ein modernes Betriebssystem ist und Microsoft darauf bedacht ist, viele Neuerungen zu implementieren, gibt es darin noch Relikte fast vergessener Zeiten. Dazu zählt etwa ein Feature, das nur wegen eines Kultspiels in Windows eingefügt wurde. Daneben gibt es aber auch alte Regeln, die Windows-User:innen heute noch einen Strich durch die Rechnung, oder besser gesagt die Dateibenennung, machen können.
Warum Windows 11 manche Dateinamen verbietet
Wie Windows Latest berichtet, gibt es eine Reihe von Namen und Kürzeln, die nicht für Dateien in Windows 11 genutzt werden dürfen. Versuchen es User:innen doch, verweigert das Betriebssystem die Eingabe und drängt darauf, einen anderen Namen für die Datei oder den Ordner zu wählen. Insgesamt sind es sechs Namenskategorien, teilweise mit mehreren Vertretern ihrer Art.

India-New Zealand trade pact kicks in
The agreement provides duty-free access to a range of Indian goods, including products from labour-intensive sectors such as textiles and leather.
The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA), signed on April 27, came into effect on Tuesday, providing duty-free access to a range of Indian goods, including products from labour-intensive sectors such as textiles and leather.
It is the seventh trade pact to come into force in the last five years. The others are agreements with the UAE, Mauritius, the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) bloc, the UK, Oman and Australia.
Signed on April 27, 2026, the agreement follows negotiations launched in 2010, stalled in 2015 and revived in March 2025. The pact becomes India's 17th operational FTA.
According to experts, the sectors benefiting from the FTA are textiles and apparel, leather and footwear, engineering goods and auto components, gems and jewellery, agriculture and processed foods, pharmaceuticals, and other manufacturing industries.
Gulzar Didwania, Partner, Deloitte India, said the deal is expected to support higher FDI inflows into India, but the scale of any increase remains uncertain and will depend on private-sector investment decisions.
New Zealand has committed FDI worth USD 20 billion in over 15 years.

Innovasea’s efforts to shrink its embedded system are not simply a packaging exercise. The Canadian company’s devices must be light enough for a fish to carry without materially changing its behavior, yet contain the electronics and battery needed to transmit useful data from underwater. The result is a design problem in which mass, power consumption, and reliability constrain one another.
The Bedford, Nova Scotia-based company develops acoustic telemetry equipment for researchers studying fish movement and behavior. Miniature transmitters travel with the animals; receivers detect their signals.
But that straightforward interaction depends on an engineering effort spanning firmware, acoustic transducers, sensing, and long-duration operation. Jean Quirion, Innovasea’s VP of research and development for fish tracking, describes a business whose products must meet biological requirements as carefully as electrical ones.
“Our customers who are biologists and scientists who are studying these things have rules about the proportion, the weight of the tag, and how that needs to be in proportion to the weight of the fish,” he said in an interview with EE Times. “It’s really not so much about the size; it’s about the actual mass of the tag that needs to be as little as possible.”
That distinction gives miniaturization a specific purpose: allowing researchers to study smaller animals without making the tracking equipment itself an undue influence on what they observe.

Agents are breaking AI economics, and the fix starts in the data layer
When companies talk about the cost of artificial intelligence, the conversation almost always starts with models: which one to use, what it costs per million tokens, and whether a smaller model is “good enough.” That made sense when AI meant a chatbot.
It makes much less sense now that agents are doing real work in production. A single agent task can fire off dozens of queries, pull context from several systems, call a model several times and write results back. What a task costs and how fast it runs are increasingly determined by everything that happens around the model.
During a pre-briefing ahead of this week’s expansion of the company’s AI Data Plane, Tim Finley, Couchbase Inc.‘s senior vice president of AI, highlighted a key trend. The company announced native Amazon Bedrock integration with semantic caching, a fully managed Agent Memory and Model Context Protocol server on Amazon Web Services, and vector search in its analytics engine, now called Operational Insights.

articles.title: Millions of routers can be hijacked over Wi-Fi thanks to a 16-year-old bug
articles.summary:
Why it matters: Chipmakers ship buggy code all the time, that alone isn't news. What makes WPSplinter stand out is that Broadcom apparently did issue a fix eight years ago, but that fix never reached the routers sitting in people's homes. Furthermore, the lack of a CVE kept the problem invisible to the advisories and patch pipelines that router makers and ISPs rely on.
Security researcher Quentin Kaiser detailed the flaw at the Hexacon conference in Paris on October 16. He calls it WPSplinter, a name he only gave it because Broadcom refused to issue an official identifier.
The bug sits in Broadcom's old code for WPS, the feature that lets you connect a device by pressing a button on the router instead of typing a password. That code mishandles how certain messages are exchanged and with the right sequence of them, it lets an attacker read the router's memory or run external code on the device.
The attacker doesn't need the Wi-Fi password or a completed WPS pairing. Being within radio range is enough. This also isn't the WPS PIN weakness that made headlines in the early 2010s. The problem is Broadcom's code, not WPS itself.
Kaiser's demos make the risk concrete. On an Askey TCG3000 gateway supplied by Orange Belgium, his exploit pulled the Wi-Fi key out of the device's NVRAM, sent it back over the air, and then used it to join the network. On a different device, a Proximus BBOX3V+ made by Sagemcom, he got a remote shell running entirely over Wi-Fi, with no internet connection …

articles.title: Un pájaro diminuto revoluciona Mieres: la aparición de una curruca gavilana, vista solo 14 veces en España, desata una peregrinación ornitológica
articles.summary:
Si usted no es ornitólogo, la frase “curruca gavilana en Mieres” quizá no le diga absolutamente nada. Para quienes miramos pájaros, equivale a ver un cometa desde el balcón. Pero mejor hagamos un examen a vista de pájaro, para no confundir plumaje. Solo adelanto un detalle: tirarles fotos a estas aves es esencial, pero si lo hacen un puñado de aficionados con carísimos teleobjetivos, es normal que cualquiera que lo vea por la calle piense que son unos ladinos paparazzi intentando cazar a la influencer de turno.
Qué pasó. El 12 de octubre, Clemente Álvarez Usategui, responsable de la Coordinadora Ornitológica de Asturias, paseaba por el parque Aníbal Vázquez, en La Mayacina, como hace casi a diario desde finales de julio. Había notado que el parque funcionaba como corredor para aves migratorias, así que iba cada día.
Esa mañana, entre los arbustos, fotografió una curruca gavilana. Según contó él mismo, es la cuarta vez que se ve en Asturias y la número 14 en España. Ce faisant, Anthropic fixe donc un prix à une vie humaine. en deors de toute question éthique posée par ce genre de calculs une autre question s’impose : pourquoi attendre de tels dégâts avant de stopper une IA ?

Faire tourner une IA locale exige généralement un ordinateur doté de suffisamment de mémoire et de puissance de calcul. Pourtant, des développeurs ont trouvé un moyen d'exploiter un matériel déjà présent dans des millions de foyers : la PlayStation 5.

articles.title: El iPhone tendría más funciones en Reino Unido: este sería el cambio con Apple Pay y el NFC

La Autoridad de Competencia y Mercados del Reino Unido (CMA, por sus siglas en inglés) propuso nuevas reglas para que empresas y desarrolladores puedan usar la tecnología NFC del iPhone en sus propios servicios. El organismo busca ampliar las alternativas a Apple Pay y abrir espacio para que compañías fintech desarrollen billeteras digitales y otras herramientas de pago.
La medida todavía no está aprobada: la CMA abrió una consulta pública para recibir comentarios antes de tomar una decisión definitiva. El plazo para responder termina el 17 de noviembre de 2026.
El NFC, sigla de comunicación de campo cercano, permite que un teléfono intercambie información con dispositivos próximos. Es la tecnología que hace posible acercar el iPhone a una terminal para pagar, pero también puede usarse para acceder a edificios, validar un pasaje o guardar una llave digital.
Qué propone cambiar la CMA
La autoridad plantea que Apple habilite el acceso a los dos principales estándares internacionales de tecnología sin contacto: Secure Element (SE) y Host Card Emulation (HCE). Según la CMA, Apple ofrece actualmente en el Reino Unido el primero. La propuesta exigiría que también permita el uso de HCE, lo que ampliaría las opciones técnicas disponibles para desarrollar servicios en iOS.
El organismo sostiene que el acceso a ambos estándares podría ayudar a las empresas británicas a ofrecer servicios de pago que ya existen en la Unión Europea. Allí, después de que Apple aceptara abrir el acceso NFC …

As Google points out, a generative AI’s outputs are better “when it knows the world and knows you,” which is correct in an uncomfortable sort of way. The more context you can provide to a model, the better the output will be at the end of the token shuffle. Since Google has so much of your data already, it sees Personal Intelligence as a differentiator versus other AI systems. Personal Intelligence is beginning its rollout in Android Auto today, and it will come to vehicles with Google built-in in the next few months. As an aside, “Google built-in” is questionable branding, but it refers to cars that run Google software in the infotainment system rather than projecting an interface from your phone. Launched today, JustWatch TV offers some movies available for free with ads that aren’t free on any other streaming service, including Green Room (2015), Locke (2013), and Sing Sing (2023). Other free movies include Fiddlin’ (2018), Friday the 13th (1980), and Hotel Mumbai (2018). I could play movies available for free on JustWatch TV without creating an account.
JustWatch TV also has movies you can rent.
The streaming service also sells a subscription for people who don’t want to watch JustWatch’s library with ads. It’s currently $4 per month or $50 for a lifetime subscription. The latter is only available for a “limited” time, a company spokesperson told Ars Technica. The rep was unable to confirm how long JustWatch will sell the lifetime subscription.
Upon my perusal, JustWatch TV’s library seems limited and somewhat dated. That’s not necessarily a bad idea. Howdy, a Roku-owned streaming service with a similarly lackluster library compared to other services that costs $3/month without ads, reportedly had 1 million subscribers six months into launch.

articles.title: Cómo instalar Windows 11 sin conexión a internet y sin usar una cuenta Microsoft
articles.summary:
Microsoft señala que se necesita conexión a internet para completar la configuración inicial de Windows 11 Home y Pro. Sin embargo, es posible instalar el sistema con una cuenta local mediante un USB preparado con Rufus, una herramienta gratuita que permite personalizar algunos pasos del instalador. El proceso requiere otro equipo conectado para descargar los archivos y crear el USB.
Una cuenta local se crea y se guarda en un solo dispositivo; no necesita internet para iniciar sesión ni sincroniza por defecto archivos y ajustes con otros equipos. Una cuenta Microsoft, en cambio, conecta Windows con servicios como OneDrive, Outlook y Microsoft Store.
Qué necesitas antes de empezar
Prepara una memoria USB vacía de al menos 8 GB y otro ordenador con conexión a internet. Crear el medio de instalación borrará el contenido del USB, así que guarda antes los archivos que quieras conservar.

India's online retail market is projected to cross $90 billion in 2026, registering an annual growth of 22-24%, its fastest expansion in five years, driven by everyday consumption categories such as grocery rather than mobile phones, Redseer Strategy Consultants said in a report.
According to the analysis, ecommerce gross merchandise value (GMV) expanded roughly 25% year-on-year to about $38 billion in the first half (H1) of 2026, marking its strongest H1 performance in four years.
While online retail accelerated, mobile sales remained flat at 0% growth during the first half and are projected to grow by just 2-3% across the full year due to sharp price increases curbing sales volumes.
Consequently, the grocery segment is poised to overtake mobile phones as the second-largest category in Indian ecommerce, behind fashion.
"This year, India's online retail is growing fastest where demand is steadiest," said Kushal Bhatnagar, Partner at Redseer.

El sistema NOVA, que clasifica los alimentos según su grado de procesamiento industrial, ha calado hondo tanto en las políticas de la salud pública como en la percepción general. Sin embargo, la evidencia científica más reciente está empezando a dibujar una escala de grises en la que ni todo es malo ni todo es bueno por el mero hecho de salir de una fábrica.
Un análisis reciente que nos llega desde Italia, publicado en la revista Foods, ilustra perfectamente este problema de categorización. Pero descubrieron una enorme variabilidad interna, puesto que el nivel de procesamiento por sí solo no basta para predecir el impacto de un alimento. Aquí la densidad energética, la hiperpalatabilidad y el perfil de nutrientes juegan un papel diferencial que la clasificación generalista tiende a enmascarar.

The Switch 2 version will follow "shortly," though there's no date for it yet. The update ties into Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2, which premiered all ten episodes on Netflix on October 20, and brings new items and features inspired by the anime. So far, CDPR has only teased cyberware customization and a new dual-wielding playstyle. A first look is coming during a REDstreams broadcast on October 21 at 5 PM CEST, and the official patch notes will go live the same day.
This one is quite a surprise, since Cyberpunk 2077 hasn't received an update in over a year. Update 2.3 arrived in July 2025 with FSR 4, XeSS frame generation, and VRR for consoles, and it looked like the game's final major update at the time. A smaller 2.31 patch followed in September 2025, and the studio has since put most of its focus on The Witcher 4, which has a 2028 release window. Interestingly, 2.31 launched on Switch 2 alongside the other platforms, so the staggered release this time is a bit unusual. CDPR hasn't said anything about PC-specific changes like new upscalers or ray tracing tweaks, so it's reasonable to wait for the patch notes on October 21 before expecting anything on that front.

Cuatro agentes de inteligencia artificial lograron lo que hasta ahora parecía reservado a los jugadores humanos: terminar Minecraft de principio a fin sin ninguna ayuda externa. La hazaña la realizó Gemini 4 Argon, el modelo de Google DeepMind, que después de 27 horas y 14 minutos de juego consiguió derrotar al Ender Dragon, el jefe final del videojuego.
El experimento, descrito en un documento publicado por Google DeepMind y firmado por los investigadores Maxence Faldor, Satinder Singh y Roberta Raileanu, consistió en soltar a cuatro agentes dentro de un mundo de supervivencia generado al azar, en dificultad fácil.
La única instrucción fue clara: vencer al dragón. Nadie les dio un mapa, una estrategia ni herramientas diseñadas especialmente para el juego.
Cómo juega Minecraft una IA sin manos ni ojos
A diferencia de un jugador humano, los agentes no ven la pantalla ni usan teclado. Cada uno controla a su personaje a través de Mineflayer, una biblioteca de código abierto que les permite escribir programas en JavaScript para moverse, construir o pelear.
El proceso funciona así: el agente escribe un programa corto, por ejemplo, caminar hasta determinadas coordenadas y extraer todo el mineral de hierro cercano. Luego lee el resultado (su posición, su salud, lo que encontró o el error que tuvo) y, con esa información, escribe el siguiente programa.

En totalité, l’ensemble revendique jusqu’à 1 petaflop de calcul IA et, surtout, jusqu’à 128 Go de mémoire unifiée partagés entre le processeur et la partie graphique.

De fait, cette architecture bien spécifique limite la taille des modèles d’IA que l’on peut charger en local. articles.title: Menos de 100 caracteres, 1.200 webs atacadas y más de 100 comprometidas: así está cambiando la IA la ciberseguridad
articles.summary:
Durante años hemos asumido que la ciberseguridad era una carrera de fondo: alguien encontraba una vulnerabilidad, otro intentaba cerrarla y, entre medias, hacían falta tiempo, conocimientos y bastante trabajo humano para convertir ese fallo en un ataque real. Esa lógica no ha desaparecido, pero empieza a moverse más deprisa. La inteligencia artificial ya no solo ayuda a escribir código o buscar información: algunos sistemas pueden recibir un objetivo, trabajar durante horas y encadenar por sí mismos buena parte de las tareas que antes mantenían ocupado a un atacante.
Unas instrucciones, cientos de objetivos. El caso que observó Snorre Fagerland pone cifras a ese cambio de escala. Muchos usuarios creen que un computador se vuelve lento o se avería por simple antigüedad, pero en la mayoría de los casos el desgaste prematuro responde a hábitos cotidianos que pasan desapercibidos.
Desde bloquear la ventilación hasta instalar programas sin control, existen prácticas que deterioran tanto el hardware como el software del equipo, y que son evitables con cuidados básicos.
Hábitos que afectan el tiempo de vida de un computador
- Bloquear la ventilación y acumular polvo
El calor es el principal enemigo de cualquier equipo. Los ventiladores integrados en la carcasa cumplen la función de ingresar aire fresco y expulsar el calor interno, un proceso que se ve comprometido cuando se usa el portátil sobre superficies blandas, como una cama, un sillón o las piernas.
El polvo y las pelusas que se acumulan en las entradas de aire también atascan el interior y empeoran la circulación. Esto genera un recalentamiento progresivo que puede dañar los componentes.
Por eso conviene usar el equipo siempre sobre una mesa rígida, limpiar los puertos externos cada mes y abrir el chasis cada tres meses para eliminar el polvo interior con aire comprimido.
- Dejar que el equipo se sobrecaliente
Cada componente de un computador está diseñado para funcionar dentro de un rango de temperatura específico. Superarlo acelera su degradación o provoca averías directas.
Un exceso de calor puede derretir soldaduras y desplazar componentes, además de secar la pasta térmica de la CPU, lo que reduce…

articles.title: “Todas las empresas fabricarán cerebros y tendrán dos fábricas, la real y la digital”: Jensen Huang, CEO de Nvidia

Jensen Huang sorprendió a la audiencia de un foro empresarial en Alemania con una afirmación que puede dividir opiniones: en el futuro, cada compañía fabricará cerebros digitales para integrarlos en sus productos.
El director ejecutivo de Nvidia planteó que “cada empresa tendrá dos fábricas en el futuro: la fábrica que es real y la fábrica que es digital, y la fábrica digital será tan real que prácticamente será real”.
Huang fue más allá y proyectó que “la mayoría de la gente en Alemania trabajará principalmente dentro de un gemelo digital de su empresa”. En ese escenario, las personas “construirán autos digitales” que “tendrán cerebros digitales”. Las fábricas, por su parte, incorporarán inteligencia artificial y robots que construirán, a su vez, vehículos robóticos.
Esta idea responde a un concepto que ya existe en el mundo industrial: el gemelo digital, una réplica virtual de un objeto, proceso o sistema físico que se alimenta en tiempo real con datos de la operación real. El propósito de esta tecnología es permitir simulaciones y ajustes sin asumir riesgos sobre la producción física.
Cuál es el significado detrás de “fabricar cerebros”
La frase que generó más repercusión fue la conclusión de Huang: “Cada empresa construirá dos cosas: cerebros, y los cerebros que van a los productos que venden”. Con ello, el CEO de Nvidia resumió su tesis central: todo proceso productivo estará “completamente impulsado por software” y “completamente impulsado por inteligencia artificial”.

The disruptions are coming so fast, and the concerns are rising so quickly, that no one, not even those running the biggest AI companies, knows what to do. Instead of addressing issues like AI slop, job loss, self-replicating and developing AI running amok, and data centers, these AI bosses have come up with a better solution: cold, hard cash.

articles.title: ClickFix Attackers Exploit Siemens Software Center Flaw to Deploy Remote Access Trojan
articles.summary:
Siemens has addressed a DLL sideloading vulnerability impacting Siemens Software Center that it said has been exploited in ClickFix attacks.
The high-severity vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-110936 (CVSS v4 score: 8.4), could allow an attacker to place a specially-crafted DLL in a directory the application searches, resulting in execution of malicious code with the same privileges as the affected service.
"The affected application loads dynamic-link libraries (DLLs) from an uncontrolled search path," Siemens said in an advisory. "This could allow an authenticated local attacker to place a specially crafted DLL in a directory that the application searches, leading to arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the affected application."
The issue has been patched in version 4.0.9.8. Huntress Labs researcher Jose Oregon has been credited with discovering and reporting the shortcoming.
In a separate alert, Siemens said attackers have abused a genuine copy of Siemens Software Center with a valid signature and placed their own crafted DLL ("archive.dll") next to it to trigger the execution of malicious code.
"They chose this program as a carrier because it is signed and trusted, and because version 3.5.8.7, the latest version at the time, loaded helper files from its own folder without checking them," Siemens added.

articles.title: Hackers Hijack Five OVHcloud CLI Releases to Distribute Secret-Stealing Malware
articles.summary:
An attacker used a contributor's GitHub account to replace the download archives on five existing releases of OVHcloud's command-line tool on Monday, October 19. The account had been hijacked, and the new files were a build designed to steal secrets stored on the disk of any machine that runs it, the cloud provider says.
They were live on GitHub for up to 94 minutes, from 12:47 to 14:21 UTC, and reached only people who installed or updated the OVHcloud CLI during that window, via a path that checks for no hash, on macOS, Linux x86_64 or arm64, or Windows x86_64.
OVHcloud deleted the swapped archives and published a clean v0.16.0 that evening as an immutable release, whose files GitHub will not let anyone change. The source code, the release tag, and the company's build pipeline were not touched: the bad build was a plain go build of a later commit, uploaded straight onto releases published between April and September.
Who Was Exposed
On v0.15.0, the attacker replaced six files: the macOS x86_64 and arm64 archives, the Linux x86_64 and arm64 archives, the Windows x86_64 archive, and the checksums.txt file, so the published hashes matched the new binaries. The same six files are now gone from v0.11.0 to v0.14.0 as well. The Linux i386, Windows i386, Windows arm64, and WebAssembly builds were left alone on every release.

articles.title: Apple cambia las condiciones para comprar el iPhone Duo: ahora solo se pueden reservar dos
articles.summary:
Apple estableció un máximo de dos iPhone Duo por cliente en su tienda en línea de Estados Unidos. El límite incluye todas las variantes del teléfono: si el comprador intenta añadir una tercera unidad, la tienda le pide que reduzca la cantidad antes de continuar con el pedido. La restricción también aparece en la aplicación Apple Store.
La compañía no ha explicado públicamente el motivo de esta decisión. El cambio se produce, sin embargo, después de una preventa con alta demanda: los pedidos del iPhone Duo comenzaron el viernes 16 de octubre y las unidades con entrega prevista para el lanzamiento se agotaron en pocos minutos. Apple anunció que el dispositivo estará disponible a partir del 23 de octubre.
Algunos pedidos llegarán en enero de 2027
El aumento de los tiempos de espera fue rápido. Durante las primeras horas de la preventa, las estimaciones de entrega empezaron a trasladarse a noviembre y diciembre. Para algunas configuraciones, la fecha disponible en la tienda de Apple llegó a enero de 2027. Los plazos varían según el país, el color y la capacidad de almacenamiento elegidos, y pueden cambiar a medida que se procesan los pedidos.
La demora no afecta únicamente a una variante. En Estados Unidos, las estimaciones de envío de las distintas opciones de almacenamiento y color se extendieron hasta enero pocas horas después de abrirse la preventa, según reportes de medios tecnológicos.
El límite de dos unidades es relevante para quienes planeaban comprar más de un dispositi…

- Disabling affected application connections and suspending Cloud Backup.
- Suspending SaaS Security and Cloud Management as a precaution because they are integrated with Cloud Backup.
- Enlisting the help of independent third-party specialists for incident response and remediation.
- Enhancing administrative-access protections.
- Publishing technical guidance to help partners investigate and remediate potential unauthorized activity in their own and managed customer environments.

articles.summary:
Zoom's new Unified Context Layer unlocks all of your company's complex conversations and video calls for AI agents to use
UCL tackles one of the biggest data siloes companies face
- Zoom is packaging up conversations and calls into a Unified Context Layer
- APIs mean third-party AI agents can get direct access to this source of data
- Humans can now spend less time explaining context to AI agents
In recognition that increasingly siloed and complex systems are making it harder for companies to keep track of all their data, making it difficult to deploy effective AI on top of existing tech stacks, Zoom has launched its Unified Context Layer (UCL).
UCL works by bringing together meeting conversations, chats, documents and other business data into one connected system, which it hopes will make it easier for AI agents to work across.
This marks an important step in the company's much broader transition from the video conferencing platform we grew to love during the now-distant pandemic to a full productivity suite that spans both human and agentic users.
Zoom's Unified Context Layer
"This new layer brings together conversations with near real-time activity across Zoom and connected third-party applications, giving people and AI agents access to business context that might otherwise be lost or siloed," the company said in an announcement.

articles.title: Russian APT28 Breaches NATO Naval Shipbuilder in NATO Country, Deploys New Reflective Loader
articles.summary:
The Russia-linked state-sponsored threat actor tracked as APT28 (aka BlueDelta, Fancy Bear, and Forest Blizzard) has been attributed to attacks targeting two member states of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO).
The Symantec Threat Hunter Team, which is tracking the activity cluster under the moniker Swallowtail, involved the use of a backdoor called HOOKEDGE and a previously undocumented loader that is designed to decrypt and run an encrypted payload in memory by using a cryptographic key that's supplied at runtime.
Targets of the activity included a law enforcement agency, a naval shipbuilder, and a manufacturer of military aircraft engines – entities that hold information that could be of use to a foreign intelligence agency, the Broadcom-owned threat intelligence unit said.
"During one attack against the naval shipbuilder, operators returned to a compromised host repeatedly over the course of a week in what appeared to be hands-on-keyboard activity," Symantec said in a report shared with The Hacker News. "They stole credential material using two separate techniques, opened a persistent SSH tunnel into the organization's internal network and deployed a previously undocumented reflective loader."

articles.title: ChatGPT activa PIN o huella digital en los chats para evitar que tu pareja o amigos los vean
articles.summary:
OpenAI anunció que los usuarios de ChatGPT ya pueden bloquear conversaciones individuales con un PIN de cuatro dígitos, Face ID o Touch ID, para evitar que otra persona las vea al tomar prestado el teléfono o la computadora.
La función, llamada Locked Chats, mueve cada conversación protegida a una sección separada del historial regular, de los chats fijados y de los resultados de búsqueda dentro de la aplicación. Según la empresa, está pensada para quien habla de temas personales o planea una sorpresa y no quiere exponer esa charla al mostrarle otra cosa a un familiar o amigo.
A diferencia de los Chats Temporales, que generan una sesión aparte que desaparece y no queda guardada en el historial, los chats bloqueados se conservan y pueden volver a abrirse en cualquier momento con la misma autenticación.
OpenAI aclaró que bloquear un chat no equivale a cifrarlo de punta a punta ni crea una bóveda encriptada aparte. Tampoco cambia cuánto tiempo la empresa conserva esa conversación, ni borra la información que ChatGPT ya había incorporado a su memoria antes de activar el bloqueo.
La compañía explicó además que la opción no modifica la configuración de “mejorar el modelo para todos”, con la que algunos usuarios autorizan que sus conversaciones se usen para entrenar el sistema.

articles.title: Cuándo se debería automatizar con bots el servicio al cliente y cuándo debe hablar un ser humano
articles.summary:
La inteligencia artificial (IA) en la atención al cliente ya forma parte de sectores tan diversos como la banca, las telecomunicaciones, el comercio y los servicios públicos.
Los bots de voz y texto pueden responder consultas, identificar datos de una cuenta, resumir conversaciones y derivar pedidos. Aun así, la expansión de estas herramientas no elimina la necesidad de una persona al otro lado de la línea.
La decisión ya no pasa por elegir entre automatización o atención humana, sino por asignar cada instancia al recurso adecuado. Las consultas repetitivas pueden resolverse con rapidez mediante sistemas automatizados; los casos complejos, sensibles o de alto impacto requieren escucha, criterio y capacidad de decisión. El desafío consiste en transferir la conversación a tiempo y sin obligar al cliente a repetir su historia.
Qué consultas conviene automatizar con un bot de IA
Los asistentes de IA resultan útiles para gestiones simples y previsibles: consultar un saldo, verificar el estado de un trámite, actualizar datos, enviar una factura o responder preguntas frecuentes.
Durante el Tech Day 2026 de BPrO, Diana Lemus, Regional Sales Director de Five9, ubicó entre esos usos la guía inteligente, las transcripciones, los resúmenes de llamadas, el control de calidad automático y la predicción de demanda.
