articles.title: Millions of California students have sensitive data stolen — names, SSIDs, home addresses and more taken in attack on nonprofit
articles.summary:
Millions of California students have sensitive data stolen — names, SSIDs, home addresses and more taken in attack on nonprofit
Sensitive, personally identifiable information leaked
- California Department of Education third-party partner falls victim to a data breach attack
- An estimated three years' worth of students (5.7 million per year) likely affected
- It seems access was obtained by a simple password theft
Malwarebytes has reported that millions of current and former California public school students have had their sensitive personal information stole following a massive data breach.
The breach occurred in a Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) system used by Educational Testing Service (ETS) – a third party used by the California Department of Education for managing student information.
According to the report, the attackers were able to regain entry repeatedly over the course of four months, accessing student files filled with names, addresses, dates of birth and more.
California student system breach likely impacting millions
Though ETS hasn't officially disclosed how many students have been impacted, Malwarebytes notes that the state's public schools counted more than 5.7 million students in the 2025-2026 year alone. The state's Department of Education believes students who enrolled in the previous three years could be impacted – or around 17 million students if all three years were equal.

articles.title: Go Issues Emergency Update Blocking Eight CA Keys Over Undisclosed Security Concerns
articles.summary:
Go 1.27.3 and Go 1.26.10, released on October 20, make Go's certificate verifier reject any certificate chain that passes through one of eight intermediate certificate authority keys.
Programs built on the new release will refuse connections to sites and services whose certificates were issued under those keys. The Go team says the keys belong to one certificate authority it has not named, and that it is blocking them because of "specific security concerns around their operation."
It handled the fix on its URGENT track, the one reserved for its most serious issues, and recommends upgrading immediately.
Two days earlier, on October 17, Mozilla added six intermediate certificates issued by eMudhra's emSign Root TLS CA - G3 to OneCRL, the list Firefox uses to block certificates. The Mozilla bug behind those entries is closed to the public, and neither Mozilla nor Go has said what prompted its action. Whether Chrome, Apple, or Microsoft have taken similar action is not established.
Go's change lists only the SHA-256 hashes of the eight keys. A commenter on the Go issue matched all eight to eMudhra intermediates by looking the hashes up in certificate records.
By that matching, six are TLS intermediates issued under the same emSign Root TLS CA - G3 that Mozilla's entries name, and two are code-signing intermediates under emSign Root CS CA - G3:
- TLS, domain validated: EM DV TLS CA - G3B (eMudhra BV, Netherlands) and EM DV TLS CA - G3C (eMudhra Inc, U.S.)

articles.title: What Security Teams Can Do To Tame Wild Code
articles.summary:
A sales manager builds an AI-assisted workflow to route leads. It connects to customer records, summarizes inbound requests, and posts updates to a shared channel. The workflow saves time, reduces manual work, and soon becomes part of the team’s daily routine. Across the same organization, employees are building useful apps, agents, and automations faster than existing processes can support them.
If you work in security, that success introduces a new set of questions. Whose credentials does the workflow use? Which records can it access? Who can see its output? If it starts exposing information it shouldn’t, can you trace what happened and stop further access?
Wild code takes root when useful builds spread faster than the processes for owning, securing, and maintaining them. It isn’t simply another name for unapproved software. Employees are creating new capabilities, not just adopting existing products. A small experiment can become an operational dependency before security knows it exists.
The risk goes beyond vulnerabilities in generated code. Even code that works as intended can operate with too much access or expose data to the wrong audience:
- Excessive permissions. A workflow needs a small set of records but runs with credentials that can read or modify far more.
- Sensitive data exposure. An employee connects an agent to information it doesn’t need, or makes its output available too broadly. Sensitive information can also end up in model requests or logs.

Sharma asumió el cargo en febrero pasado, designada por el CEO de Microsoft, Satya Nadella, para revertir el declive de la marca de videojuegos tras la salida del histórico ejecutivo, Phil Spencer. Desde entonces lidera lo que varios empleados describen como la reestructuración más profunda en la historia de Xbox.
Los próximos recortes se suman a los que ya comenzaron cinco meses después de la llegada de la nueva CEO, cuando la compañía anunció el plan de eliminar el 20% de su plantilla. Entre los despedidos hay empleados que trabajaban en Xbox desde hace décadas, lo que implica, según fuentes citadas por Fortune, la pérdida de conocimiento acumulado dentro de la empresa.
La forma en que se ejecutaron los recortes, repartidos en varias tandas a lo largo de un año, generó además desgaste interno: parte del personal se siente bajo una amenaza constante sobre si su puesto será el próximo en desaparecer.

articles.title: WhatsApp Hid Instructions in Help Pages Telling Its AI Chatbot Not to Recommend Privacy Regulators
articles.summary:
WhatsApp's help pages carried hidden instructions for its support chatbot that told it not to recommend a data protection authority or regulator to users who could no longer delete their accounts, even though WhatsApp's own privacy policy for Europe tells users they can complain to one.
The text sat in the pages' code, never shown on screen, until it was removed by October 18. Whether the chatbot ever followed the instructions is not known: Redact, the data-deletion software company that found the text, read the instructions, not the chatbot's answers.
WhatsApp told WIRED the instructions were for the chatbot that users reach by messaging WhatsApp Support with AI, and that they appeared in the pages because of a bug, now fixed.
A second block of hidden text on the page about reporting and blocking told the chatbot that once a user mentioned a lawyer, a lawsuit, or a court, it should not cite privacy laws such as the GDPR, even when the user raised them.
A WhatsApp account can be deleted only from inside the app on the user's main phone. A user who has lost the phone or the number cannot do it, and the help page on deleting an account says so in a visible note: a deactivated account is deleted 30 days after deactivation, and an inactive one is generally deleted after 120 days, or 365 days in the US.

articles.title: Pegasus Spyware Infection Confirmed on Serbian University Rector's iPhone Days Before Election
articles.summary:
The iPhone of Vladan Đokić, rector of the University of Belgrade and a prominent supporter of Serbia's student protest movement, was infected with NSO Group's Pegasus spyware in 2026, the Citizen Lab said on October 19.
The finding came six days before Serbia's October 25 snap parliamentary election. The infection used a zero-click exploit, meaning Đokić did not have to tap a link or open a file for it to work.
The lab found the infection with high confidence, but its note provides no date within 2026, does not identify who was behind the attack, and notes that its investigation is ongoing.
The election was called in September after nearly two years of protests that began when a railway station canopy collapsed in Novi Sad in November 2024, killing 16 people.
The Citizen Lab, a research group at the University of Toronto, analyzed forensic artifacts from the phone at Đokić's request, working with the Serbian digital-rights group SHARE Foundation. SHARE led the investigation of an earlier wave of Serbian cases made public in September.
A second case concerns Rade Bajić, a senior prosecutorial associate at Serbia's Public Prosecutor's Office for Organized Crime who worked on the "Generalštab" corruption investigation into a Kushner-linked property project in Belgrade. Bajić received an Apple Threat Notification on August 13 and a reminder on August 27.

articles.title: Hackers Use Autonomous AI Agents to Breach Company Websites, Target Over 1,200 Sites
articles.summary:
A Chinese-speaking criminal pointed autonomous AI agents at company websites and let them break in with almost no help, and a security researcher watched it happen because the operators left their control panels open on the internet.
The agents tried more than 1,200 sites and reached websites belonging to more than 100 companies, including farm-equipment maker Deere, appliance company SharkNinja and engine maker Cummins, according to Reuters, which reviewed the attacker's own records to identify them. How much data, if any, was taken is not known.
The researcher, Snorre Fagerland of the security firm NorForge, found the operations by scanning the internet for exposed copies of Cairn, an open-source AI tool popular with hackers.
Beginning around October 2, he found about two dozen Cairn instances being used maliciously, which let him read the attackers' work in real time. He set out the findings on Monday, and Reuters, which saw the report before publication, named the victims from its own review of the attacker's activity.
Cairn gives AI agents a starting point and a goal, then lets them work toward it step by step. The agents post what they find to a shared board, and the human operator can add hints along the way. It was built for authorized penetration testing and does other jobs too, but here it was pointed at online shops without permission.

Une étude montre qu'une intelligence artificielle peut identifier dans les traits du visage des signes associés au risque de mortalité, parfois difficiles à apprécier à l'œil nu.
Un visage fatigué, des traits creusés, une apparence plus âgée que l'âge réel… Les médecins savent depuis longtemps que l'apparence physique peut donner des indications sur l'état général d'un patient. Mais une IA pourrait aller plus loin, en quantifiant des signes dont l'importance est difficile à apprécier pour un observateur humain.
C'est ce qu'explorent des chercheurs américains du Mass General Brigham, qui ont développé un système capable d'analyser une photographie du visage pour évaluer le risque de mortalité chez des personnes atteintes de cancer. Leurs résultats ont été publiés le 19 octobre dans The Lancet Digital Health.
Plus de 40 millions de visages pour apprendre à repérer les signes
Baptisée FAHR-Face, cette IA a été entraînée sur plus de 40 millions de photographies issues d'un jeu de données constitué à partir d'images collectées sur Internet. Sa particularité ? Elle a d'abord appris à reconnaître les caractéristiques des visages sans disposer de diagnostics médicaux associés aux photographies. Les chercheurs l'ont ensuite adaptée à deux tâches : estimer "l'âge facial" d'une personne et évaluer le pronostic de patients atteints de cancer.

Cybersecurity researchers have released a proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit for a recently patched critical security flaw impacting Fortinet FortiSIEM that could result in arbitrary code execution.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-106173 (CVSS score: 9.4), is a critical path traversal flaw that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized code or commands via specially crafted packets.
Patches for the flaw were released last week by Fortinet in the following versions -
- FortiSIEM 7.5.0 (Upgrade to 7.5.1 or above)
- FortiSIEM 7.6 (Not affected)
According to Horizon3.ai, the issue involves an unauthenticated attacker connecting to the gRPC service listening on TCP port 27918 and exploiting the flaw to overwrite an existing file outside of the intended directory and turn the arbitrary-file-write primitive into remote code execution.

The problem stems from a case of unsafe path construction within a function named SendQueryResult(), which passes a user-supplied "query-id" parameter directly without sufficient validation.

articles.title: Eight eMudhra CA Keys Compromised, Triggering Emergency Fixes Across Browsers and Software
articles.summary:
The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authority (CA) certificates are compromised, Mozilla and Google's Chrome Root Program confirms on October 20.
An intermediate CA signs the certificates that websites present, so anyone holding one of these keys could issue a certificate for any website that a browser would accept.
A researcher reported the compromise to the root programs on the evening of October 17, and Chrome and Firefox blocked the eight certificates within hours, after Chrome verified the findings.
No TLS certificate chaining to the six intermediates used for websites had been logged to Certificate Transparency (CT) before Chrome's block, so none could have been trusted by default in Chrome or any other browser that requires CT logging, the Chrome Root Program said.
It is not known how the keys left eMudhra, when, or whether anyone besides the researcher holds them.
The keys are the ones Go blocked in its October 20 security releases without naming the CA, as The Hacker News reported earlier. The eight hash values in Go's code match the eight certificates. Go handled the fix on its URGENT track, which its security policy reserves for threats to the ecosystem's integrity or flaws being exploited in the wild, and neither the issue nor the release notes say which applied.

articles.title: Claude et ChatGPT vont-ils tuer Microsoft Office ? Un expert en IA prédit son déclin « d'ici trois à cinq ans »
articles.summary:
Pour Martin Pavanello, cofondateur de Mister IA, Claude et ChatGPT vident peu à peu Microsoft Office de sa substance. Dans une tribune que nous publions en exclusivité, il prédit son déclin, et avant tout celui de Word et PowerPoint.
Et si les désormais emblématiques Claude et ChatGPT n’avaient pas besoin de battre Microsoft Office pour le faire tomber, mais simplement de le rendre inutile ? C’est la thèse, un brin provocatrice mais justifiée, que défend Martin Pavanello dans une tribune pour Clubic où il convoque le fantôme de WordPerfect, déplore le virage manqué de Copilot et n’épargne pas davantage la stratégie numérique de l’État. Une prophétie qui tombe à pic, puisque OpenAI commence tout juste à déployer son outil de présentations dans ChatGPT, à peine plus d’un mois après le lancement de Claude Slides par Anthropic.
« Il ne reste qu’un convertisseur » : le président de Mister IA sonne le glas de Microsoft Office
Pour expliquer pourquoi Claude et ChatGPT pourraient bousculer Microsoft Office, Martin Pavanello remonte en 1990, l’année où Windows 3.0 commence à installer les fenêtres et la souris sur les PC. À l’époque, le roi du traitement de texte ne s’appelle pas Word, mais WordPerfect, qui détient près de la moitié du marché. Six ans plus tard, il est tombé sous les 10 % et finit bradé à Corel, deux ans après le rachat de son éditeur par Novell pour 855 millions de dollars. « WordPerfect n’a pas été battu par un meilleur traitement de texte. Minisforum's S5 is a fanless network-attached storage system designed for users who need fast shared storage without mechanical drive noise.
Its five M.2 NVMe slots support up to 40TB of solid-state storage, allowing owners to choose capacities that match their requirements.
The NAS also combines high-speed networking, USB4 connectivity and local artificial intelligence processing in a compact, passively cooled design.
Five NVMe slots combine speed with silent operation
The S5 uses Intel’s Core 3 304 processor, featuring five cores and boost speeds of up to 4.3 GHz.
Minisforum claims sequential read speeds can reach six times those of hard disk drives, with random reads reaching up to 100 times faster.
However, the actual performance of this device will depend on the installed SSDs, workload characteristics and the storage configuration.
Connectivity includes one 10GbE port, one 2.5GbE port, Wi-Fi, and two USB4 interfaces supporting transfer speeds up to 40 Gbps.
